title.zh: 卷三百二十七 列傳第八十六 王安石子:雱 附:唐坰 王安禮 王安國
title.en: Volume 327 Biographies 86: Wang Anshi and Son: Pang, Relative: Tang Jiong, Wang Anli, Wang Anguo
title.raw: 卷三百二十七 列傳第八十六 王安石子:雱 附:唐坰 王安禮 王安國 Volume 327 Biographies 86: Wang Anshi and Son: Pang, Relative: Tang Jiong, Wang Anli, Wang Anguo

sentences.zh: 王安石

translations.literal: Wang Anshi
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi

sentences.zh: 王安石，字介甫，撫州臨川人。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi, styled Jiefu, was a native of Linchuan in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi, styled Jiefu, was a native of Linchuan in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 父益，都官員外郎。

translations.literal: His father Yi was an Outer Gentleman of the Bureau of Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi served as an Outer Gentleman of the Bureau of Palace Attendants.

sentences.zh: 安石少好讀書，一過目終身不忘。

translations.literal: Anshi from youth loved reading; once he read something, he never forgot it for life.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Wang Anshi loved to read, and what he read once he remembered for life.

sentences.zh: 其屬文動筆如飛，初若不經意，既成，見者皆服其精妙。

translations.literal: When he composed prose his brush moved like flight; at first it seemed careless, but when finished, all who saw it admired its refinement.
translations.idiomatic: When he wrote, his brush moved swiftly; at first his work seemed effortless, but when finished, all who read it admired its brilliance.

sentences.zh: 友生曾鞏攜以示歐陽修，修為之延譽。

translations.literal: His friend Zeng Gong brought his writings to show Ouyang Xiu, and Xiu spread his reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His friend Zeng Gong brought his writings to Ouyang Xiu, who praised him widely.

sentences.zh: 擢進士上第，簽書淮南判官。

translations.literal: He was selected as a jinshi of the highest rank and appointed as a signing clerk and vice prefect of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination at the top rank and was appointed signing clerk and vice prefect of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 舊制，秩滿許獻文求試館職，安石獨否。

translations.literal: By old regulation, when one's term expired one was permitted to submit writings to seek a test for an academy post; Anshi alone refused.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, officials whose terms had expired could submit writings to qualify for an academy post; Wang Anshi alone refused.

sentences.zh: 再調知鄞縣，起堤堰，決陂塘，為水陸之利；

translations.literal: On a second transfer he was made prefect of Yin County, where he raised dikes and dams and opened reservoirs and ponds for the benefit of water and land transport.
translations.idiomatic: On his next appointment he served as prefect of Yin County, where he built dikes and dams and opened reservoirs and ponds to benefit both land and water transport.

sentences.zh: 貸穀與民，出息以償，俾新陳相易，邑人便之。

translations.literal: He lent grain to the people and took interest in repayment, enabling new and old grain to be exchanged, to the convenience of the district.
translations.idiomatic: He lent grain to the people and collected interest on repayment, allowing new grain to replace old stores; the people of the district found this a great convenience.

sentences.zh: 通判舒州。

translations.literal: He served as vice prefect of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice prefect of Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 文彥博為相，薦安石恬退，乞不次進用，以激奔競之風。

translations.literal: When Wen Yanbo was chief minister, he recommended Anshi for his quiet withdrawal and asked that he be promoted out of turn to stir up the spirit of frantic competition.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Yanbo was chief minister, he recommended Wang Anshi for his modest withdrawal from office and asked that he be promoted out of turn to counter the prevailing rush for advancement.

sentences.zh: 尋召試館職，不就。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned to test for an academy post, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to qualify for an academy post but declined.

sentences.zh: 修薦為諫官，以祖母年高辭。

translations.literal: Xiu recommended him as a remonstrating official, but he declined on the grounds that his grandmother was advanced in years.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu recommended him for a remonstrance post, but he declined because his grandmother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 修以其須祿養言於朝，用為群牧判官，請知常州。

translations.literal: Xiu spoke to the court that he needed salary to support his family, and he was made a vice prefect of the Pasturage Commission and requested appointment as prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu told the court that Wang Anshi needed an income to support his family; he was made a vice prefect of the Pasturage Commission and requested appointment as prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 移提點江東刑獄，入為度支判官，時嘉祐三年也。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be intendant of judicial prisons in Jiangdong, then entered the capital as vice director of the Revenue Commission; this was in the third year of Jiayou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as intendant of judicial prisons in Jiangdong, then entered the capital as vice director of the Revenue Commission; this was in 1058.

sentences.zh: 安石議論高奇，能以辨博濟其說，果于自用，慨然有矯世變俗之志。

translations.literal: Anshi's discourse was lofty and singular; he could support his arguments with eloquent breadth, was resolute in trusting himself, and had a stirring ambition to reform the age and transform custom.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi's arguments were bold and original; he could bolster them with eloquent learning, was resolute in following his own judgment, and harbored a passionate ambition to reform society and transform custom.

sentences.zh: 於是上萬言書，以為：「今天下之財力日以困窮，風俗日以衰壞，患在不知法度，不法先王之政故也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial of ten thousand words, stating: Today the empire's wealth and strength grow daily more exhausted, and custom grows daily more decayed; the trouble lies in not knowing law and institutions, in not taking the government of the former kings as law.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he submitted a ten-thousand-word memorial, arguing: "The empire's wealth and strength grow daily more strained, and public morals grow daily more corrupt. The root of the trouble is ignorance of law and institutions—failure to take the governance of the ancient kings as our model.

sentences.zh: 法先王之政者，法其意而已。

translations.literal: To take the government of the former kings as law is only to take their intent as law.
translations.idiomatic: To follow the governance of the ancient kings is to follow their intent, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 法其意，則吾所改易更革，不至乎傾駭天下之耳目，囂天下之口，而固已合先王之政矣。

translations.literal: If one takes their intent as law, then what I would change and reform would not need to overturn and startle the ears and eyes of all under Heaven or clamor the mouths of all under Heaven, yet would already accord with the government of the former kings.
translations.idiomatic: If we follow their intent, the changes and reforms I propose need not shock the whole realm or provoke universal outcry, yet would already accord with the governance of the ancient kings.

sentences.zh: 因天下之力以生天下之財，取天下之財以供天下之費，自古治世，未嘗以財不足為公患也，患在治財無其道爾。

translations.literal: Employ the strength of all under Heaven to produce the wealth of all under Heaven; take the wealth of all under Heaven to supply the expenses of all under Heaven. From antiquity in well-governed ages, public trouble has never been insufficient wealth; the trouble lies in having no proper way to manage wealth.
translations.idiomatic: We should use the empire's strength to generate its wealth and its wealth to meet its expenses. In well-governed ages since antiquity, insufficient revenue has never been the state's chief problem; the problem has always been the lack of a proper method for managing finances.

sentences.zh: 在位之人才既不足，而閭巷草野之間亦少可用之才，社稷之託，封疆之守，陛下其能久以天幸為常，而無一旦之憂乎？

translations.literal: Talent among those in office is already insufficient, and among lanes and alleys and the wild countryside there are also few usable talents. The trust of the altars of soil and grain, the defense of the frontiers—can Your Majesty long take Heaven's favor as the norm and be without worry for a single day?
translations.idiomatic: There is already too little talent among those in office, and too few capable men even among common people in town and country. Can Your Majesty long rely on Heaven's favor alone to safeguard the altars of state and defend the frontiers, without fear of sudden disaster?

sentences.zh: 願監苟且因循之弊，明詔大臣，為之以漸，期合於當世之變。

translations.literal: I wish that Your Majesty would observe the evils of complacency and routine, clearly instruct the great ministers, and act by degrees, expecting to accord with the changes of the present age.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty observe the evils of complacency and inertia, clearly instruct your chief ministers, and proceed step by step toward meeting the demands of our own age.

sentences.zh: 臣之所稱，流俗之所不講，而議者以為迂闊而熟爛者也。」

translations.literal: What your servant speaks of is what vulgar custom does not discuss, and what critics consider remote and broad and stale.
translations.idiomatic: What I propose is what common opinion ignores, and what critics dismiss as impractical and threadbare."

sentences.zh: 後安石當國，其所注措，大抵皆祖此書。

translations.literal: Later when Anshi directed the state, his measures and arrangements were for the most part modeled on this memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Wang Anshi directed the state, most of his policies were modeled on this memorial.

sentences.zh: 俄直集賢院。

translations.literal: Soon he was made director of the Jixian Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed director of the Jixian Academy.

sentences.zh: 先是，館閣之命屢下，安石屢辭；

translations.literal: Earlier, appointments to the academies and institutes had been issued repeatedly, and Anshi had repeatedly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, appointments to the academies and institutes had been issued repeatedly, and Wang Anshi had repeatedly declined them.

sentences.zh: 士大夫謂其無意於世，恨不識其面，朝廷每欲俾以美官，惟患其不就也。

translations.literal: Officials and gentry said he had no interest in the world and regretted not knowing him in person; the court whenever it wished to grant him a fine office feared only that he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and officials said he had no interest in public office and regretted not knowing him personally; the court, whenever it wished to grant him a fine post, feared only that he would refuse.

sentences.zh: 明年，同修起居注，辭之累日。

translations.literal: The next year he was made concurrent compiler of the Daily Record, and he declined for many days.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed concurrent compiler of the Daily Record and declined for many days.

sentences.zh: 閣門吏齎敕就付之，拒不受；

translations.literal: A gate clerk brought the edict to deliver to him, but he refused to accept it.
translations.idiomatic: A gate clerk brought the edict to deliver to him, but he refused to accept it.

sentences.zh: 吏隨而拜之，則避於廁；

translations.literal: The clerk followed and bowed to him, whereupon he withdrew to the privy.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk followed and bowed to him; he withdrew to the privy.

sentences.zh: 吏置敕於案而去，又追還之；

translations.literal: The clerk placed the edict on the desk and left, then was sent back to retrieve it.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk placed the edict on the desk and left, then was sent back to retrieve it.

sentences.zh: 上章至八九，乃受。

translations.literal: He submitted memorials seven or eight or nine times before he finally accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted seven or eight memorials of refusal before finally accepting.

sentences.zh: 遂知制誥，糾察在京刑獄，自是不復辭官矣。

translations.literal: He was then made drafter of edicts and inspector of capital judicial prisons, and from then on he no longer declined office.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made drafter of edicts and inspector of capital judicial prisons, and from then on he no longer declined office.

sentences.zh: 有少年得鬥鶉，其儕求之不與，恃與之昵，輒持去，少年追殺之。

translations.literal: A youth obtained a fighting quail; his companions asked for it and he would not give it; one who relied on being close to him simply took it away, and the youth pursued and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: A youth obtained a fighting quail. When his companions asked for it he refused; one who counted on their intimacy simply took it away, and the youth pursued and killed him.

sentences.zh: 開封當此人死，安石駁曰：「按律，公取、竊取皆為盜。

translations.literal: Kaifeng sentenced this man to death; Anshi objected, saying: According to law, open taking and secret taking are both theft.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng sentenced this man to death. Wang Anshi objected: "Under the law, both open seizure and secret theft count as robbery.

sentences.zh: 此不與而彼攜以去，是盜也；

translations.literal: This one did not give it and that one carried it away—this is theft.
translations.idiomatic: When one refused to give it and the other carried it away, that was theft.

sentences.zh: 追而殺之，是捕盜也，雖死當勿論。」

translations.literal: Pursuing and killing him is capturing a thief; even if death results, it should not be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing and killing him was apprehending a thief; even though the man died, no punishment should apply."

sentences.zh: 遂劾府司失入。

translations.literal: Thereupon he impeached the prefectural office for an erroneous judgment.
translations.idiomatic: He then impeached the prefectural office for an erroneous judgment.

sentences.zh: 府官不伏，事下審刑、大理，皆以府斷為是。

translations.literal: The prefectural officials did not submit; the matter was sent down to the Office of Review of Punishments and the Court of Judicial Review, and both held the prefecture's judgment correct.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural officials would not accept this; the case was referred to the Office of Review of Punishments and the Court of Judicial Review, both of which upheld the prefecture's judgment.

sentences.zh: 詔放安石罪，當詣閣門謝。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned Anshi's offense and ordered him to go to the Gate Office to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: An edict pardoned Wang Anshi's offense and ordered him to go to the Gate Office to apologize.

sentences.zh: 安石言：「我無罪。」

translations.literal: Anshi said: I am not guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said, "I am not guilty."

sentences.zh: 不肯謝。

translations.literal: He refused to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to apologize.

sentences.zh: 御史舉奏之，置不問。

translations.literal: The censorate memorialized against him, but the matter was set aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate memorialized against him, but the matter was set aside without inquiry.

sentences.zh: 時有詔舍人院無得申請除改文字，安石爭之曰：「審如是，則舍人不得復行其職，而一聽大臣所為，自非大臣欲傾側而為私，則立法不當如此。

translations.literal: At the time there was an edict that the Secretariat Academy might not request changes to appointment documents; Anshi contested it, saying: If it is truly so, then the secretaries can no longer perform their duties and must simply obey whatever the great ministers do; unless the great ministers wish to lean and act for private ends, legislation should not be made in this way.
translations.idiomatic: At the time an edict forbade the Secretariat Academy from requesting changes to appointment documents. Wang Anshi objected: "If this stands, secretaries can no longer perform their duties and must simply defer to whatever the chief ministers do. Unless the chief ministers intend to bend the law for private ends, legislation should not be made this way.

sentences.zh: 今大臣之弱者不敢為陛下守法；

translations.literal: Today the weak among the great ministers dare not uphold the law for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Today the weaker chief ministers dare not uphold the law for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 而強者則挾上旨以造令，諫官、御史無敢逆其意者，臣實懼焉。」

translations.literal: While the strong ones rely on the imperial intent to create orders, and remonstrating officials and censors none dare oppose their will—I am truly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: While the stronger ones invoke imperial intent to issue orders, and no remonstrance official or censor dares oppose them—I am truly alarmed."

sentences.zh: 語皆侵執政，由是益與之忤。

translations.literal: His words all encroached on those in power, and from this he grew ever more at odds with them.
translations.idiomatic: His words all encroached on those in power, and from this he grew ever more at odds with them.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去，終英宗世，召不起。

translations.literal: He left office on account of mourning for his mother; through the reign of Emperor Yingzong he was summoned but did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother; throughout Emperor Yingzong's reign he was summoned but did not accept.

sentences.zh: 一日講席，群臣退，帝留安石坐，曰：「有欲與卿從容論議者。」

translations.literal: One day at the lecture session, after the ministers withdrew, the emperor kept Anshi seated and said: There is something I wish to discuss with you at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: One day at the lecture session, after the ministers withdrew, the emperor kept Wang Anshi seated and said, "There is something I wish to discuss with you at leisure."

sentences.zh: 因言：「唐太宗必得魏徵，劉備必得諸葛亮，然後可以有為，二子誠不世出之人也。」

translations.literal: He then said: Emperor Taizong of Tang had to obtain Wei Zheng, and Liu Bei had to obtain Zhuge Liang, before they could accomplish anything; these two men were truly men not born in ordinary ages.
translations.idiomatic: He then said, "Emperor Taizong of Tang needed Wei Zheng, and Liu Bei needed Zhuge Liang, before they could accomplish anything. Those two men were truly unmatched in their age."

sentences.zh: 安石曰：「陛下誠能為堯，舜，則必有皋、夔、稷、禹；

translations.literal: Anshi said: If Your Majesty can truly be Yao and Shun, then there will surely be Gao Yao, Kui, Hou Ji, and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said, "If Your Majesty can truly be like Yao and Shun, then you will surely have men like Gao Yao, Kui, Hou Ji, and Yu.

sentences.zh: 誠能為高宗，則必有傅說。

translations.literal: If you can truly be Gaozong, then there will surely be Fu Yue.
translations.idiomatic: If you can truly be like Gaozong, then you will surely have a Fu Yue.

sentences.zh: 彼二子皆有道者所羞，何足道哉？

translations.literal: Those two men are what men of the Way would be ashamed of—what is there to speak of?
translations.idiomatic: Those two men are men that the truly wise would disdain—what is there to speak of?

sentences.zh: 以天下之大，人民之眾，百年承平，學者不為不多。

translations.literal: Given the vastness of all under Heaven, the multitude of the people, a century of peace, and no lack of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Given the vastness of the empire, the multitude of its people, a century of peace, and no lack of scholars.

sentences.zh: 然常患無人可以助治者，以陛下擇術未明，推誠未至，雖有皋、夔、稷、禹、傅說之賢，亦將為小人所蔽，卷懷而去爾。」

translations.literal: Yet one constantly worries that there is no one who can assist in governance, because Your Majesty's choice of method is not yet clear and your extension of sincerity has not yet reached its fullness; even if there were worthies like Gao Yao, Kui, Hou Ji, Yu, and Fu Yue, they would still be obscured by petty men and would wrap up their talents and leave.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you constantly lament that no one can assist in governance—because Your Majesty has not yet clearly chosen your method or fully extended your sincerity. Even if there were worthies like Gao Yao, Kui, Hou Ji, Yu, and Fu Yue, petty men would still obscure them, and they would withdraw their talents and leave."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「何世無小人，雖堯、舜之時，不能無四凶。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: In what age are there no petty men? Even in the time of Yao and Shun, one could not be without the Four Evils.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "In what age are there no petty men? Even in the time of Yao and Shun there were the Four Evils."

sentences.zh: 安石曰：「惟能辨四凶而誅之，此其所以為堯、舜也。

translations.literal: Anshi said: Only by being able to distinguish the Four Evils and execute them is this why they were Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said, "It was precisely because they could distinguish the Four Evils and execute them that they were Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 若使四凶得肆其讒慝，則皋、夔、稷、禹亦安肯苟食其祿以終身乎？」

translations.literal: If the Four Evils were allowed to unleash their slander and wickedness, then how would Gao Yao, Kui, Hou Ji, and Yu be willing to eat their salaries in idleness for life?
translations.idiomatic: If the Four Evils had been allowed to unleash their slander and wickedness, how would Gao Yao, Kui, Hou Ji, and Yu have been willing to draw salary in idleness for the rest of their lives?"

sentences.zh: 登州婦人惡其夫寢陋，夜以刃斮之，傷而不死。

translations.literal: A woman of Dengzhou despised her husband's ugly appearance; at night she hacked at him with a blade, wounding but not killing him.
translations.idiomatic: A woman of Dengzhou despised her husband's ugly appearance; at night she hacked at him with a blade, wounding but not killing him.

sentences.zh: 獄上，朝議皆當之死，安石獨援律辨證之，為合從謀殺傷，減二等論。

translations.literal: When the case came up, court opinion unanimously held she should die; Anshi alone cited the law and argued that it constituted joint conspiracy to kill and wound, and should be sentenced with two degrees of reduction.
translations.idiomatic: When the case came up, court opinion unanimously held she should die; Wang Anshi alone cited the law and argued that it constituted joint conspiracy to kill and wound, warranting a sentence reduced by two degrees.

sentences.zh: 帝從安石說，且著為令。

translations.literal: The emperor followed Anshi's view and moreover established it as a regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted Wang Anshi's view and established it as a regulation.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year he was appointed Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year he was appointed Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 上謂曰：「人皆不能知卿，以為卿但知經術，不曉世務。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to him: People all fail to understand you and think you know only classical learning and do not understand affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to him, "People fail to understand you; they think you know only classical learning and do not understand affairs of state."

sentences.zh: 安石對曰：「經術正所以經世務，但後世所謂儒者，大抵皆庸人，故世俗皆以為經術不可施於世務爾。」

translations.literal: Anshi replied: Classical learning is precisely for managing affairs of the age; it is only that what later ages call Confucians are for the most part mediocre men, so vulgar custom thinks classical learning cannot be applied to affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi replied, "Classical learning exists precisely to govern affairs of state. It is only that what later ages call Confucians are for the most part mediocre men, so common opinion holds that classical learning cannot be applied to affairs of state."

sentences.zh: 上問：「然則卿所施設以何先？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked: Then what will you put first in what you implement?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Then what will you put first in what you implement?"

sentences.zh: 安石曰：「變風俗，立法度，正方今之所急也。」

translations.literal: Anshi said: Transforming custom and establishing laws and institutions are precisely what is urgent today.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said, "Transforming custom and establishing laws and institutions are precisely what is urgent today."

sentences.zh: 上以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是設制置三司條例司，令判知樞密院事陳升之同領之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Fiscal Policy Commission was established, with Chen Shengzhi, who held concurrent authority over the Bureau of Military Affairs, appointed to direct it jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Fiscal Policy Commission was established, with Chen Shengzhi, who held concurrent authority over the Bureau of Military Affairs, appointed to direct it jointly.

sentences.zh: 安石令其黨呂惠卿預其事。

translations.literal: Anshi had his partisan Lü Huiqing participate in its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi had his ally Lü Huiqing participate in its affairs.

sentences.zh: 而農田水利、青苗、均輸、保甲、免役、市易、保馬、方田諸役相繼並興，號為新法，遣提舉官四十餘輩，頒行天下。

translations.literal: Then the policies of farmland and waterworks, Green Sprouts, balanced delivery, baojia, exemption from corvée, market exchange, horse breeding, and square fields were successively launched together, called the New Policies; more than forty supervising officials were dispatched to promulgate them throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Then the policies on farmland and waterworks, Green Sprouts loans, balanced delivery, baojia militia, exemption from corvée, market exchange, horse breeding, and square-field land assessment were launched in succession, collectively called the New Policies; more than forty supervising officials were dispatched to promulgate them throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 青苗法者，以常平糴本作青苗錢，散與人戶，令出息二分，春散秋斂。

translations.literal: The Green Sprouts Law used the grain reserves of the Ever-Normal Granaries as Green Sprouts funds, distributed to households, and required interest of two parts in ten, dispersed in spring and collected in autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Green Sprouts Law, grain reserves from the Ever-Normal Granaries were converted into Green Sprouts funds, distributed to households at twenty percent interest, disbursed in spring and collected in autumn.

sentences.zh: 均輸法者，以發運之職改為均輸，假以錢貨，凡上供之物，皆得徙貴就賤，用近易遠，預知在京倉庫所當辦者，得以便宜蓄買。

translations.literal: The balanced delivery law changed the transport-assignment office into balanced delivery, lending money and goods; all tribute goods might move from expensive to cheap regions and use what was near to replace what was far; knowing in advance what the capital granaries and storehouses must supply, one could conveniently stock and purchase.
translations.idiomatic: The balanced delivery law transformed the transport-assignment office into a balanced-delivery system, lending money and goods so that all tribute goods could be procured where prices were low rather than high, using nearby sources to replace distant ones; knowing in advance what the capital granaries must supply, officials could conveniently stock and purchase as needed.

sentences.zh: 保甲之法，籍鄉村之民，二丁取一，十家為保，保丁皆授以弓弩，教之戰陣。

translations.literal: The baojia law registered the people of villages and countryside, taking one from every two adult males, grouping ten households into a bao; all bao militiamen were given bows and crossbows and taught battle formations.
translations.idiomatic: Under the baojia system, rural people were registered, one man taken from every two adult males, ten households forming a bao; all bao militiamen were given bows and crossbows and trained in battle formations.

sentences.zh: 免役之法，據家貲高下，各令出錢雇人充役，下至單丁、女戶，本來無役者，亦一概輸錢，謂之助役錢。

translations.literal: The exemption-from-corvée law, according to the high or low wealth of each household, required each to pay money to hire people to perform corvée; down to single adult males and female-headed households who originally had no corvée duty, all alike paid money, called assistance-for-corvée money.
translations.idiomatic: Under the exemption-from-corvée law, households paid money according to their wealth to hire others to perform corvée; even single adult males and female-headed households who originally owed no corvée duty had to pay, in what was called assistance-for-corvée money.

sentences.zh: 市易之法，聽人賒貸縣官財貨，以田宅或金帛為抵當，出息十分之二，過期不輸，息外每月更加罰錢百分之二。

translations.literal: The market exchange law permitted people to borrow on credit the goods and wealth of the district government, using fields, houses, or gold and silk as security, with interest of two parts in ten; if payment was overdue, each month an additional penalty of two percent was added beyond the interest.
translations.idiomatic: Under the market exchange law, people could borrow government goods and funds on credit, using land, houses, or gold and silk as security at twenty percent interest; if payment was overdue, an additional two-percent penalty was added each month beyond the interest.

sentences.zh: 保馬之法，凡五路義保願養馬者，戶一匹，以監牧見馬給之，或官與其直，使自市，歲一閱其肥瘠，死病者補償。

translations.literal: The horse-breeding law: in all five circuits, righteous bao who wished to raise horses received one horse per household, given from horses held by the pasturage commission, or the government gave them the price to buy their own; once a year their fatness or leanness was inspected, and for dead or sick horses compensation was required.
translations.idiomatic: Under the horse-breeding law, in all five circuits, baojia militia who wished to raise horses received one horse per household, supplied from horses held by the pasturage commission, or the government gave them the price to buy their own; once a year the horses' condition was inspected, and compensation was required for dead or sick animals.

sentences.zh: 方田之法，以東、西、南、北各千步，當四十一頃六十六畝一百六十步為一方，歲以九月，令、佐分地計量，驗地土肥瘠，定其色號，分為五等，以地之等，均定稅數。

translations.literal: The square-field law took one thousand paces east, west, south, and north, equaling forty-one qing, sixty-six mu, and one hundred sixty paces as one square; each year in the ninth month, magistrates and assistants divided the land and measured it, tested the fertility or barrenness of the soil, fixed color codes, divided it into five grades, and according to the grade of the land uniformly fixed tax amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Under the square-field law, a square of one thousand paces on each side—forty-one qing, sixty-six mu, and one hundred sixty paces—was taken as one unit; each year in the ninth month, magistrates and assistants measured and divided the land, assessed soil fertility, assigned color codes in five grades, and fixed tax amounts according to land grade.

sentences.zh: 又有免行錢者，約京師百物諸行利入厚薄，皆令納錢，與免行戶祗應。

translations.literal: There was also exemption-from-service money: estimating the thick or thin profits of the various guilds of the hundred goods in the capital, all were required to pay money in exchange for exempting service households from attendance duties.
translations.idiomatic: There was also exemption-from-service money: estimating the profits of the various guilds handling goods in the capital, all were required to pay money in exchange for exempting service households from attendance duties.

sentences.zh: 自是四方爭言農田水利，古陂廢堰，悉務興復。

translations.literal: From this the four directions competed in speaking of farmland and waterworks; ancient reservoirs and abandoned dams were all zealously restored.
translations.idiomatic: From this officials everywhere competed to report on farmland and waterworks; ancient reservoirs and abandoned dams were zealously restored.

sentences.zh: 又令民封狀增價以買坊場，又增茶監之額，又設措置河北糴便司，廣積糧穀於臨流州縣，以備饋運。

translations.literal: The people were also ordered to submit sealed bids at increased prices to buy monopoly shops; tea supervision quotas were increased; the Hebei Grain Purchase Convenience Office was established; grain was widely stored in prefectures and counties along rivers to prepare for transport supply.
translations.idiomatic: The people were also ordered to submit sealed bids at increased prices to buy monopoly shops; tea supervision quotas were increased; the Hebei Grain Purchase Convenience Office was established; and grain was widely stored in riverine prefectures and counties to prepare for transport supply.

sentences.zh: 由是賦斂愈重，而天下騷然矣。

translations.literal: From this taxation grew ever heavier, and all under Heaven was in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: From this taxation grew ever heavier, and the realm was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞呂誨論安石過失十事，帝為出誨，安石薦呂公著代之。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Lü Hui memorialized on ten faults of Anshi; the emperor removed Hui on his account, and Anshi recommended Lü Gongshu to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Lü Hui memorialized on ten faults of Wang Anshi; the emperor removed Hui on his account, and Wang Anshi recommended Lü Gongshu to replace him.

sentences.zh: 韓琦諫疏至，帝感悟，欲從之，安石求去。

translations.literal: When Han Qi's remonstrance memorial arrived, the emperor was moved and wished to follow it; Anshi asked to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Qi's remonstrance memorial arrived, the emperor was moved and wished to follow it; Wang Anshi asked to leave office.

sentences.zh: 司馬光答詔，有「士夫沸騰，黎民騷動」之語，安石怒，抗章自辨，帝為巽辭謝，令呂惠卿諭旨，韓絳又勸帝留之。

translations.literal: Sima Guang in reply to an edict used the words 'officials seething, the common people in turmoil'; Anshi was angry and submitted a memorial in self-defense; the emperor offered conciliatory words of apology, had Lü Huiqing convey the imperial intent, and Han Jiang again urged the emperor to keep him.
translations.idiomatic: In reply to an edict Sima Guang wrote that 'officials were seething and the common people in turmoil'; Wang Anshi was angry and submitted a memorial in self-defense; the emperor offered conciliatory words of apology, had Lü Huiqing convey the imperial intent, and Han Jiang again urged the emperor to keep him.

sentences.zh: 安石入謝，因為上言中外大臣、從官、臺諫、朝士朋比之情，且曰：「陛下欲以先王之正道勝天下流俗，故與天下流俗相為重輕。

translations.literal: Anshi entered to give thanks and thereupon spoke to the emperor of the factional collusion among inner and outer great ministers, attendant officials, censorate remonstrators, and court gentlemen, saying: Your Majesty wishes to use the correct Way of the former kings to overcome the vulgar custom of all under Heaven, and so you and the vulgar custom of all under Heaven counterbalance each other.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi entered to give thanks and spoke to the emperor of factional collusion among ministers inside and outside the court, attendant officials, censorate remonstrators, and court gentlemen, saying, "Your Majesty wishes to use the correct Way of the ancient kings to overcome the vulgar custom of the realm, and so you and that vulgar custom counterbalance each other.

sentences.zh: 流俗權重，則天下之人歸流俗；

translations.literal: If vulgar custom's weight is heavy, then the people of all under Heaven turn to vulgar custom.
translations.idiomatic: If vulgar custom weighs heavier, then the people of the realm turn to vulgar custom.

sentences.zh: 陛下權重，則天下之人歸陛下。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty's weight is heavy, then the people of all under Heaven turn to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty weighs heavier, then the people of the realm turn to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 權者與物相為重輕，雖千鈞之物，所加損不過銖兩而移。

translations.literal: Weight counterbalances things; even for a thing of a thousand jun, what is added or subtracted need be no more than a zhu or a liang to shift it.
translations.idiomatic: Weight counterbalances things; even for a load of a thousand jun, adding or subtracting no more than a zhu or a liang can shift the balance.

sentences.zh: 今奸人欲敗先王之正道，以沮陛下之所為。

translations.literal: Now wicked men wish to defeat the correct Way of the former kings to obstruct what Your Majesty is doing.
translations.idiomatic: Now wicked men wish to defeat the correct Way of the ancient kings to obstruct what Your Majesty is doing.

sentences.zh: 於是陛下與流俗之權適爭輕重之時，加銖兩之力，則用力至微，而天下之權，已歸於流俗矣，此所以紛紛也。」

translations.literal: Thus when Your Majesty and vulgar custom are just contending over weight, if one adds the force of a zhu or a liang, though the force applied is extremely slight, the weight of all under Heaven already turns to vulgar custom—this is why there is such clamor.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when Your Majesty and vulgar custom are just contending over weight, if you add even the force of a zhu or a liang, though the effort is tiny, the weight of the realm already shifts to vulgar custom—this is why there is such clamor."

sentences.zh: 上以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 安石乃視事，琦說不得行。

translations.literal: Anshi then resumed his duties, and Qi's proposal could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi then resumed his duties, and Qi's proposal could not be carried out.

sentences.zh: 安石與光素厚，光援朋友責善之義，三詒書反覆勸之，安石不樂。

translations.literal: Anshi and Guang had long been close; Guang invoked the duty of friends to admonish one another and three times sent letters repeatedly urging him; Anshi was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi and Sima Guang had long been close; Guang invoked the duty of friends to admonish one another and three times sent letters repeatedly urging him; Wang Anshi was displeased.

sentences.zh: 帝用光副樞密，光辭未拜而安石出，命遂寢。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to use Guang as vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Guang declined before accepting the appointment, and when Anshi left office the order was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to appoint Guang vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Guang declined before accepting the appointment, and when Wang Anshi left office the order was shelved.

sentences.zh: 公著雖為所引，亦以請罷新法出潁州。

translations.literal: Although Gongshu had been brought in by him, he also asked to abolish the New Policies and went out to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Although Gongshu had been brought in by him, he also asked to abolish the New Policies and was sent out to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 御史劉述、劉琦、錢顗、孫昌齡、王子韶、程顥、張戩、陳襄、陳薦、謝景溫、楊繪、劉摯，諫官范純仁、李常、孫覺、胡宗愈皆不得其言，相繼去。

translations.literal: Censors Liu Shu, Liu Qi, Qian Yi, Sun Changling, Wang Zishao, Cheng Hao, Zhang Jian, Chen Xiang, Chen Jian, Xie Jingwen, Yang Hui, and Liu Zhi, and remonstrators Fan Chunren, Li Chang, Sun Jue, and Hu Zongyu all failed to get their words heeded and left office one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Liu Shu, Liu Qi, Qian Yi, Sun Changling, Wang Zishao, Cheng Hao, Zhang Jian, Chen Xiang, Chen Jian, Xie Jingwen, Yang Hui, and Liu Zhi, and remonstrators Fan Chunren, Li Chang, Sun Jue, and Hu Zongyu all failed to get their words heeded and left office one after another.

sentences.zh: 驟用秀州推官李定為御史，知制誥宋敏求、李大臨、蘇頌封還詞頭，御史林旦、薛昌朝、范育論定不孝，皆罷逐。

translations.literal: Li Ding, a judicial officer of Xiuzhou, was abruptly used as censor; drafters Song Minqiu, Li Dalin, and Su Song sealed and returned the appointment documents; censors Lin Dan, Xue Changchao, and Fan Yu argued that Ding was unfilial—all were dismissed and expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ding, a judicial officer of Xiuzhou, was abruptly appointed censor; drafters Song Minqiu, Li Dalin, and Su Song sealed and returned the appointment documents; censors Lin Dan, Xue Changchao, and Fan Yu argued that Ding was unfilial—all were dismissed and expelled.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士范鎮三疏言青苗，奪職致仕。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Fan Zhen three times memorialized on Green Sprouts, was stripped of office, and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Fan Zhen three times memorialized against Green Sprouts loans, was stripped of office, and retired.

sentences.zh: 惠卿遭喪去，安石未知所託，得曾布，信任之，亞于惠卿。

translations.literal: Huiqing left on account of mourning; Anshi did not know whom to entrust affairs to, obtained Zeng Bu, trusted him, and ranked him second only to Huiqing.
translations.idiomatic: When Huiqing left to mourn, Wang Anshi did not know whom to entrust affairs to; he obtained Zeng Bu, trusted him, and ranked him second only to Huiqing.

sentences.zh: 三年十二月，拜同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year he was appointed Associate Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the third year he was appointed Associate Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 明年春，京東、河北有烈風之異，民大恐。

translations.literal: The next spring in Jingdong and Hebei there were violent winds as an anomaly, and the people were greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring violent winds struck Jingdong and Hebei, and the people were greatly terrified.

sentences.zh: 帝批付中書，令省事安靜以應天變，放遣兩路募夫，責有司、郡守不以上聞者。

translations.literal: The emperor annotated and sent it to the Secretariat, ordering the provincial offices to keep quiet to respond to Heaven's change, discharging conscripted laborers on both circuits, and holding responsible officials and prefects who had not reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent instructions to the Secretariat ordering provincial offices to restore calm in response to Heaven's warning, discharging conscripted laborers on both circuits and holding responsible any officials or prefects who had failed to report upward.

sentences.zh: 安石執不下。

translations.literal: Anshi held to his position and would not issue it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi held to his position and refused to issue the order.

sentences.zh: 開封民避保甲，有截指斷腕者，知府韓維言之，帝問安石，安石曰：「此固未可知，就令有之，亦不足怪。

translations.literal: Kaifeng people to avoid baojia service cut off fingers and sever wrists; Prefect Han Wei reported it; the emperor asked Anshi, and Anshi said: This is indeed not yet knowable; even if it exists, it is not enough to be strange.
translations.idiomatic: To avoid baojia service, people in Kaifeng cut off fingers and severed wrists. Prefect Han Wei reported this; when the emperor asked Wang Anshi, he said, "This is hard to verify; even if it were true, it would not be surprising.

sentences.zh: 今士大夫睹新政，尚或紛然驚異；

translations.literal: Today when officials and gentry see the new policies, they still sometimes clamor in alarm and wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Today when officials and gentry see the new policies, they still sometimes clamor in alarm and wonder.

sentences.zh: 況于二十萬戶百姓，固有惷愚為人所惑動者，豈應為此遂不敢一有所為邪？」

translations.literal: How much more among two hundred thousand households of common people—surely there are the stupid and foolish who are moved by others—should one for this reason not dare to do anything at all?
translations.idiomatic: How much more among two hundred thousand households of common people—surely some foolish ones are swayed by others—should we for this reason not dare to act at all?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「民言合而聽之則勝，亦不可不畏也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: When the people's words are gathered and listened to, one prevails; one also cannot fail to fear them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When the people's words are gathered and heeded, one prevails—but one also cannot fail to respect them."

sentences.zh: 東明民或遮宰相馬訴助役錢，安石白帝曰：「知縣賈蕃乃范仲淹之婿，好附流俗，致民如是。」

translations.literal: People of Dongming sometimes blocked the chief minister's horse to complain about assistance-for-corvée money; Anshi told the emperor: Magistrate Jia Fan is the son-in-law of Fan Zhongyan and likes to attach himself to vulgar custom, causing the people to be like this.
translations.idiomatic: People of Dongming sometimes blocked the chief minister's horse to complain about assistance-for-corvée money. Wang Anshi told the emperor, "Magistrate Jia Fan is Fan Zhongyan's son-in-law; he likes to pander to popular opinion, which is why the people behave this way."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「治民當知其情偽利病，不可示姑息。

translations.literal: He also said: In governing the people one should know their true and false conditions and their benefits and harms; one cannot show indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "In governing the people one must know their true conditions and their grievances; one cannot show indulgence.

sentences.zh: 若縱之使妄經省臺，鳴鼓邀駕，恃眾僥倖，則非所以為政。」

translations.literal: If one indulges them to recklessly pass through the provincial and central offices, beat drums to intercept the imperial carriage, and rely on the crowd for lucky advantage, then this is not the way to govern.
translations.idiomatic: If one indulges them to recklessly petition the provincial and central offices, beat drums to intercept the imperial carriage, and rely on mob pressure for advantage, that is not the way to govern."

sentences.zh: 其強辯背理率類此。

translations.literal: His forceful argument against reason was generally of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His forceful arguments against reason were generally of this kind.

sentences.zh: 帝用韓維為中丞，安石憾曩言，指為善附流俗以非上所建立，因維辭而止。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to use Han Wei as censor-in-chief; Anshi resented his earlier words and pointed out that he was good at attaching himself to vulgar custom to oppose what the emperor had established; because Wei declined, the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to appoint Han Wei censor-in-chief; Wang Anshi resented his earlier words and accused him of pandering to popular opinion to oppose what the emperor had established; because Wei declined, the appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修乞致仕，馮京請留之，安石曰：「修附麗韓琦，以琦為社稷臣。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu asked to retire; Feng Jing asked to keep him; Anshi said: Xiu attached himself to Han Qi and treated Qi as a pillar of state.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu asked to retire; Feng Jing asked to keep him. Wang Anshi said, "Xiu attached himself to Han Qi and treated Qi as a pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 如此人，在一郡則壞一郡，在朝廷則壞朝廷，留之安用？」

translations.literal: A man like this, in one commandery ruins one commandery, at court ruins the court—what use is there in keeping him?
translations.idiomatic: A man like this ruins whatever commandery he is in and ruins the court when he is at court—what use is there in keeping him?"

sentences.zh: 乃聽之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was permitted to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was permitted to retire.

sentences.zh: 富弼以格青苗解使相，安石謂不足以阻奸，至比之共、鯀。

translations.literal: Fu Bi resigned his commissioner-grand-councillor post by blocking Green Sprouts; Anshi said this was insufficient to obstruct wickedness and even compared him to Gong and Gun.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi resigned his commissioner-grand-councillor post by blocking Green Sprouts; Wang Anshi said this was insufficient to obstruct wickedness and even compared him to Gong and Gun.

sentences.zh: 靈臺郎尤瑛言天久陰，星失度，宜退安石，即黥隸英州。

translations.literal: Gentleman of the Spirit Terrace You Ying said Heaven had long been overcast and the stars had lost their measure, and Anshi should be removed; he was immediately tattooed and made a bondsman in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman of the Spirit Terrace You Ying said Heaven had long been overcast and the stars had lost their measure, and Wang Anshi should be removed; he was immediately tattooed and made a bondsman in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 唐坰本以安石引薦為諫官，因請對極論其罪，謫死。

translations.literal: Tang Jiong had originally been recommended by Anshi as a remonstrating official; he then requested an audience and argued to the utmost his crimes, and was demoted and died.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jiong had originally been recommended by Wang Anshi as a remonstrating official; he then requested an audience and argued his crimes to the utmost, and was demoted and died.

sentences.zh: 文彥博言市易與下爭利，致華嶽山崩。

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo said market exchange competed with the people for profit and caused Mount Hua to collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo said market exchange competed with the people for profit and caused Mount Hua to collapse.

sentences.zh: 安石曰：「華山之變，殆天意為小人發。

translations.literal: Anshi said: The change at Mount Hua was perhaps Heaven's intent, raised on behalf of petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said, "The change at Mount Hua was perhaps Heaven's intent, raised on behalf of petty men.

sentences.zh: 市易之起，自為細民久困，以抑兼併爾，于官何利焉。」

translations.literal: The rise of market exchange was itself because common people had long been distressed, to suppress consolidation—what profit is there for the government?
translations.idiomatic: Market exchange was instituted because common people had long been distressed, to suppress consolidation—what profit is there for the government?"

sentences.zh: 閼其奏，出彥博守魏。

translations.literal: He blocked the memorial and sent Yanbo out to guard Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He blocked the memorial and sent Yanbo out as prefect of Wei.

sentences.zh: 於是呂公著、韓維，安石藉以立聲譽者也；

translations.literal: Thus Lü Gongshu and Han Wei, whom Anshi had relied on to establish his reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Lü Gongshu and Han Wei, whom Wang Anshi had relied on to establish his reputation.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修、文彥博，薦己者也；

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu and Wen Yanbo, who had recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu and Wen Yanbo, who had recommended him.

sentences.zh: 富弼、韓琦，用為侍從者也；

translations.literal: Fu Bi and Han Qi, who had used him as an attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi and Han Qi, who had used him as an attendant.

sentences.zh: 司馬光、范鎮，交友之善者也：悉排斥不遺力。

translations.literal: Sima Guang and Fan Zhen, good friends—all were expelled without sparing effort.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang and Fan Zhen, good friends—all were expelled without sparing effort.

sentences.zh: 禮官議正太廟太祖東向之位，安石獨定議還僖祖於祧廟，議者合爭之，弗得。

translations.literal: Ritual officials debated correcting Taizu's east-facing position in the Grand Ancestral Temple; Anshi alone fixed the decision to return Xizu to the distant temple; debaters together contested it but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials debated correcting Taizu's east-facing position in the Grand Ancestral Temple; Wang Anshi alone decided to return Xizu to the distant temple; debaters contested it together but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 上元夕，從駕乘馬入宣德門，衛士訶止之，策其馬。

translations.literal: On the Lantern Festival evening, following the imperial procession he rode a horse into Xuande Gate; guards shouted to stop him and whipped his horse.
translations.idiomatic: On the Lantern Festival evening, while following the imperial procession he rode a horse into Xuande Gate; guards shouted to stop him and whipped his horse.

sentences.zh: 安石怒，上章請逮治。

translations.literal: Anshi was angry and submitted a memorial requesting arrest and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi was angry and submitted a memorial requesting arrest and punishment.

sentences.zh: 御史蔡確言：「宿衛之士，拱扈至尊而已，宰相下馬非其處，所應訶止。」

translations.literal: Censor Cai Que said: Palace guards merely stand in attendance on the sovereign; a chief minister dismounting was not their place—they properly shouted to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Cai Que said, "Palace guards merely stand in attendance on the sovereign; a chief minister riding where he should dismount was properly stopped."

sentences.zh: 帝卒為杖衛士，斥內侍，安石猶不平。

translations.literal: The emperor finally had the guards beaten with rods and expelled the inner attendants, but Anshi was still dissatisfied.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor finally had the guards beaten with rods and expelled the inner attendants, but Wang Anshi was still dissatisfied.

sentences.zh: 王韶開熙河奏功，帝以安石主議，解所服玉帶賜之。

translations.literal: Wang Shao opened the Xihe region and reported merit; the emperor, because Anshi had led the deliberation, removed the jade belt he was wearing and bestowed it on him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao opened the Xihe region and reported merit; because Wang Anshi had led the deliberation, the emperor removed the jade belt he was wearing and bestowed it on him.

sentences.zh: 七年春，天下久旱，饑民流離，帝憂形於色，對朝嗟歎，欲盡罷法度之不善者。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year, drought had long afflicted all under Heaven, starving people wandered in exile, worry showed on the emperor's face, he sighed at court, and wished to abolish entirely the bad parts of laws and institutions.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year drought had long afflicted the realm; starving people wandered in exile; worry showed on the emperor's face; he sighed at court and wished to abolish entirely the harmful parts of the new laws.

sentences.zh: 安石曰：「水旱常數，堯、湯所不免，此不足招聖慮，但當修人事以應之。」

translations.literal: Anshi said: Flood and drought are regular occurrences that even Yao and Tang could not avoid; this is insufficient to draw the sage's concern—one need only cultivate human affairs to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said, "Flood and drought are regular occurrences that even Yao and Tang could not avoid; this is not worth the sage's concern—one need only cultivate human affairs to respond."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此豈細事，朕所以恐懼者，正為人事之未修爾。

translations.literal: The emperor said: How is this a small matter? What I fear is precisely that human affairs have not been cultivated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "How is this a small matter? What I fear is precisely that human affairs have not been properly managed.

sentences.zh: 今取免行錢太重，人情咨怨，至出不遜語。

translations.literal: Now the collection of exemption-from-service money is too heavy; popular sentiment complains and resents, even to the point of uttering disrespectful words.
translations.idiomatic: Now the collection of exemption-from-service money is too heavy; popular sentiment complains and resents, even to the point of uttering disrespectful words.

sentences.zh: 自近臣以至后族，無不言其害。

translations.literal: From close ministers to the empress's kin, none failed to speak of its harm.
translations.idiomatic: From close ministers to the empress's kin, none failed to speak of its harm.

sentences.zh: 兩宮泣下，憂京師亂起，以為天旱，更失人心。」

translations.literal: The two palaces wept, fearing disorder would rise in the capital, thinking that with Heaven's drought they would lose popular hearts even more.
translations.idiomatic: The two palaces wept, fearing disorder would rise in the capital, thinking that with Heaven's drought they would lose popular support even more."

sentences.zh: 安石曰：「近臣不知為誰，若兩宮有言，乃向經、曹佾所為爾。」

translations.literal: Anshi said: I do not know which close ministers; if the two palaces spoke, it was the doing of Xiang Jing and Cao Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said, "I do not know which close ministers; if the two palaces spoke, it was the doing of Xiang Jing and Cao Yi."

sentences.zh: 馮京曰：「臣亦聞之。」

translations.literal: Feng Jing said: Your servant also heard it.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jing said, "Your servant also heard it."

sentences.zh: 安石曰：「士大夫不逞者以京為歸，故京獨聞其言，臣未之聞也。」

translations.literal: Anshi said: Unruly officials and gentry take Jing as their refuge, so Jing alone heard their words; your servant did not hear them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said, "Unruly officials and gentry take Jing as their refuge, so Jing alone heard their words; I did not hear them."

sentences.zh: 監安上門鄭俠上疏，繪所見流民扶老攜幼困苦之狀，為圖以獻，曰：「旱由安石所致。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Gate of Peaceful Rule Zheng Xia submitted a memorial, painting the distressed condition of refugees he saw supporting the old and leading the young, making a picture to present, saying: The drought was caused by Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor of the Gate of Peaceful Rule Zheng Xia submitted a memorial, painting the distressed condition of refugees he saw supporting the old and leading the young, making a picture to present, saying, "The drought was caused by Wang Anshi.

sentences.zh: 去安石，天必雨。」

translations.literal: Remove Anshi and Heaven will surely rain.
translations.idiomatic: Remove Wang Anshi and Heaven will surely rain."

sentences.zh: 俠又坐竄嶺南。

translations.literal: Xia was again punished by exile to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Xia was again punished by exile to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 慈聖、宣仁二太后流涕謂帝曰：「安石亂天下。」

translations.literal: Empress Dowagers Cisheng and Xuanren wept and said to the emperor: Anshi has thrown all under Heaven into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowagers Cisheng and Xuanren wept and said to the emperor, "Wang Anshi has thrown the realm into disorder."

sentences.zh: 帝亦疑之，遂罷為觀文殿大學士、知江寧府，自禮部侍郎超九轉為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: The emperor also doubted him and thereupon removed him as Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and prefect of Jiangning, leapfrogging nine ranks from Vice Minister of Rites to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also doubted him and thereupon removed him as Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and prefect of Jiangning, leapfrogging nine ranks from Vice Minister of Rites to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 呂惠卿服闋，安石朝夕汲引之，至是，白為參知政事，又乞召韓絳代己。

translations.literal: When Lü Huiqing's mourning period ended, Anshi drew him in morning and evening; at this time he recommended him as Vice Grand Councillor and also asked to summon Han Jiang to replace himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Huiqing's mourning period ended, Wang Anshi drew him in morning and evening; at this time he recommended him as Vice Grand Councillor and also asked to summon Han Jiang to replace himself.

sentences.zh: 二人守其成謨，不少失，時號絳為「傳法沙門」，惠卿為「護法善神」。

translations.literal: The two men kept to his established plans without much deviation; at the time Jiang was called the 'Dharma-transmitting monk' and Huiqing the 'Dharma-protecting good spirit.'
translations.idiomatic: The two men kept to his established plans without much deviation; at the time Jiang was called the 'Dharma-transmitting monk' and Huiqing the 'Dharma-protecting good spirit.'

sentences.zh: 而惠卿實欲自得政，忌安石復來，因鄭俠獄陷其弟安國，又起李士寧獄以傾安石。

translations.literal: But Huiqing in fact wished to take power himself, feared Anshi's return, used the Zheng Xia case to trap his younger brother Anguo, and also raised the Li Shining case to topple Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: But Huiqing in fact wished to take power himself, feared Wang Anshi's return, used the Zheng Xia case to trap his younger brother Anguo, and also raised the Li Shining case to topple Wang Anshi.

sentences.zh: 絳覺其意，密白帝請召之。

translations.literal: Jiang perceived his intent and secretly told the emperor, asking to summon him back.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang perceived his intent and secretly told the emperor, asking to summon Wang Anshi back.

sentences.zh: 八年二月，復拜相，安石承命，即倍道來。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year he was again appointed chief minister; Anshi accepted the order and immediately came by double marches.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighth year he was again appointed chief minister; Wang Anshi accepted the order and immediately came by forced marches.

sentences.zh: 《三經義》成，加尚書左僕射兼門下侍郎，以子雱為龍圖閣直學士。

translations.literal: When the Three Classics with Commentary was completed, he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery; his son Pang was made Direct Academician of the Hall of Dragon Images.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Classics with Commentary was completed, he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery; his son Pang was made Direct Academician of the Hall of Dragon Images.

sentences.zh: 雱辭，惠卿勸帝允其請，由是嫌隙愈著。

translations.literal: Pang declined; Huiqing urged the emperor to grant his request, and from this mutual suspicion grew ever more evident.
translations.idiomatic: Pang declined; Huiqing urged the emperor to grant his request, and from this mutual suspicion grew ever more evident.

sentences.zh: 惠卿為蔡承禧所擊，居家俟命。

translations.literal: Huiqing was attacked by Cai Chengxi and stayed home awaiting orders.
translations.idiomatic: Huiqing was attacked by Cai Chengxi and stayed home awaiting orders.

sentences.zh: 雱風御史中丞鄧綰，復彈惠卿與知華亭縣張若濟為奸利事，置獄鞫之，惠卿出守陳。

translations.literal: Pang incited Censor-in-Chief Deng Wan and again impeached Huiqing and Magistrate of Huating County Zhang Ruoji for corrupt profit; a case was set up to interrogate them, and Huiqing went out to guard Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Pang incited Censor-in-Chief Deng Wan to again impeach Huiqing and Magistrate of Huating County Zhang Ruoji for corrupt profit; a case was set up to interrogate them, and Huiqing was sent out as prefect of Chen.

sentences.zh: 十月，彗出東方，詔求直言，及詢政事之未協於民者。

translations.literal: In the tenth month a comet appeared in the east; an edict sought forthright speech and inquired about governmental affairs not in accord with the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month a comet appeared in the east; an edict sought forthright speech and inquired about governmental affairs not in accord with the people.

sentences.zh: 安石率同列疏言：「晉武帝五年，彗出軫；

translations.literal: Anshi led his colleagues in a memorial saying: In the fifth year of Emperor Wu of Jin, a comet appeared in Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi led his colleagues in a memorial saying, "In the fifth year of Emperor Wu of Jin, a comet appeared in Zhen.

sentences.zh: 十年，又有孛。

translations.literal: In the tenth year there was again a broom star.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year there was again a broom star.

sentences.zh: 而其在位二十八年，與《乙巳占》所期不合。

translations.literal: Yet he reigned twenty-eight years, not matching what the Yisi Prognostications expected.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he reigned twenty-eight years, not matching what the Yisi Prognostications expected.

sentences.zh: 蓋天道遠，先王雖有官占，而所信者人事而已。

translations.literal: Heaven's Way is distant; though the former kings had official divination, what they trusted was human affairs alone.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's Way is distant; though the ancient kings had official divination, what they trusted was human affairs alone.

sentences.zh: 天文之變無窮，上下傅會，豈無偶合。

translations.literal: Astronomical changes are endless; above and below attach and combine—how could there not be chance correspondences?
translations.idiomatic: Astronomical changes are endless; above and below people attach meanings—how could there not be chance correspondences?

sentences.zh: 周公、召公，豈欺成王哉。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao—would they deceive King Cheng?
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao—would they deceive King Cheng?

sentences.zh: 其言中宗享國日久，則曰『嚴恭寅畏，天命自度，治民不敢荒寧』。

translations.literal: When they spoke of Zhongzong's long enjoyment of the state, they said: 'Solemn and reverent, in awe of Heaven's mandate, measuring himself—governing the people he dared not be negligent in repose.'
translations.idiomatic: When they spoke of Zhongzong's long reign, they said, 'Solemn and reverent, in awe of Heaven's mandate, measuring himself—governing the people he dared not be negligent in repose.'

sentences.zh: 其言夏、商多歷年所，亦曰『德』而已。

translations.literal: When they spoke of Xia and Shang lasting many years, they also said 'virtue' alone.
translations.idiomatic: When they spoke of Xia and Shang lasting many years, they also spoke only of 'virtue.'

sentences.zh: 裨灶言火而驗，欲禳之，國僑不聽，則曰『不用吾言，鄭又將火』。

translations.literal: Pi Zao spoke of fire and it was verified; wishing to avert it, Zichan would not listen, so he said: 'If you do not use my words, Zheng will again have fire.'
translations.idiomatic: Pi Zao spoke of fire and it came true; wishing to avert it, Zichan would not listen, so he said, 'If you do not use my words, Zheng will again have fire.'

sentences.zh: 僑終不聽，鄭亦不火。

translations.literal: Zichan in the end would not listen, and Zheng also did not have fire.
translations.idiomatic: Zichan in the end would not listen, and Zheng did not burn.

sentences.zh: 有如裨灶，未免妄誕，況今星工哉？

translations.literal: Even one like Pi Zao could not avoid being wild and absurd—how much more today's star officials?
translations.idiomatic: Even one like Pi Zao could not avoid being wild and absurd—how much more today's star officials?

sentences.zh: 所傳占書，又世所禁，謄寫偽誤，尤不可知。

translations.literal: The prognostic texts handed down were also banned by the age; copied with forgeries and errors, they were especially unknowable.
translations.idiomatic: The prognostic texts handed down were also banned by the age; copied with forgeries and errors, they were especially unreliable.

sentences.zh: 陛下盛德至善，非特賢于中宗，周、召所言，則既閱而盡之矣，豈須愚瞽復有所陳。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's flourishing virtue is utmost good, not merely surpassing Zhongzong; what the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao spoke of, you have already examined and exhausted—why need foolish blind men again to state anything?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's flourishing virtue is utmost good, not merely surpassing Zhongzong; what the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao spoke of, you have already examined and fulfilled—why need foolish blind men to state anything again?

sentences.zh: 竊聞兩宮以此為憂，望以臣等所言，力行開慰。」

translations.literal: I have privately heard the two palaces worry over this; I hope Your Majesty will earnestly use what your servants have said to open and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: I have privately heard the two palaces worry over this; I hope Your Majesty will earnestly use what we have said to reassure and comfort them."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「聞民間殊苦新法。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: I hear the people suffer greatly from the New Policies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I hear the people suffer greatly from the New Policies."

sentences.zh: 安石曰：「祁寒暑雨，民猶怨咨，此無庸恤。」

translations.literal: Anshi said: In cold and heat, in drought and rain, the people still complain—this need not be worried over.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said, "In cold and heat, in drought and rain, the people still complain—this need not be worried over."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「豈若並祁寒暑雨之怨亦無邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: Would it not be better to have no complaints even about cold and heat, drought and rain?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Would it not be better to have no complaints even about cold and heat, drought and rain?"

sentences.zh: 安石不悅，退而屬疾臥，帝慰勉起之。

translations.literal: Anshi was displeased, withdrew and claimed illness and lay down; the emperor consoled and urged him to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi was displeased, withdrew and claimed illness; the emperor consoled and urged him to rise.

sentences.zh: 其黨謀曰：「今不取上素所不喜者暴進用之，則權輕，將有窺人間隙者。」

translations.literal: His partisans plotted, saying: If now one does not abruptly advance and use those the emperor has always disliked, then power will be light and there will be those who spy for openings among people.
translations.idiomatic: His partisans plotted, saying, "If we do not now abruptly advance and use those the emperor has always disliked, our power will be weakened and others will spy for openings."

sentences.zh: 安石是其策。

translations.literal: Anshi approved this plan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi approved this plan.

sentences.zh: 帝喜其出，悉從之。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased at his emergence and followed it all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased at his return and followed it all.

sentences.zh: 時出師安南，諜得其露布，言：「中國作青苗、助役之法，窮困生民。

translations.literal: At the time troops were sent against Annam; spies obtained their proclamation, which said: China has made Green Sprouts and assistance-for-corvée laws that exhaust and distress the living people.
translations.idiomatic: At the time troops were sent against Annam; spies obtained their proclamation, which said, "China has made Green Sprouts and assistance-for-corvée laws that exhaust and distress the living people.

sentences.zh: 我今出兵，欲相拯濟。」

translations.literal: I now send out troops wishing to rescue and relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: I now send out troops wishing to rescue and relieve them."

sentences.zh: 安石怒，自草敕榜詆之。

translations.literal: Anshi was angry and personally drafted an edict and placard to denounce them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi was angry and personally drafted an edict and placard to denounce them.

sentences.zh: 華亭獄久不成，雱以屬門下客呂嘉問、練亨甫共議，取鄧綰所列惠卿事，雜他書下制獄，安石不知也。

translations.literal: The Huating case long failed to conclude; Pang entrusted it to his retainers Lü Jiawen and Lian Hengfu to discuss together; they took the matters Deng Wan had listed against Huiqing, mixed them with other documents, and sent them down to the imperial prison; Anshi did not know.
translations.idiomatic: The Huating case long failed to conclude; Pang entrusted it to his retainers Lü Jiawen and Lian Hengfu; they took the matters Deng Wan had listed against Huiqing, mixed them with other documents, and sent them down to the imperial prison without Wang Anshi's knowledge.

sentences.zh: 省吏告惠卿于陳，惠卿以狀聞，且訟安石曰：「安石盡棄所學，隆尚縱橫之末數，方命矯令，罔上要君。

translations.literal: A provincial clerk reported to Huiqing in Chen; Huiqing reported the matter and also sued Anshi, saying: Anshi has entirely abandoned what he learned, exalting and honoring the petty arts of the strategists, defying orders and falsifying commands, deceiving and coercing the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial clerk reported to Huiqing in Chen; Huiqing reported the matter and also sued Wang Anshi, saying, "Wang Anshi has entirely abandoned what he learned, exalting the petty arts of the strategists, defying orders and falsifying commands, deceiving and coercing the ruler.

sentences.zh: 此數惡力行於年歲之間，雖古之失志倒行而逆施者，殆不如此。」

translations.literal: These several evils were forcefully practiced within a few years; even those of old who lost their purpose and acted perversely and inversely were probably not like this.
translations.idiomatic: These evils were forcefully practiced within a few years; even those of old who lost their purpose and acted perversely were probably not like this."

sentences.zh: 又發安石私書曰：「無使上知」者。

translations.literal: He also exposed Anshi's private letter saying: Do not let the emperor know.
translations.idiomatic: He also exposed Wang Anshi's private letter saying, "Do not let the emperor know."

sentences.zh: 帝以示安石，安石謝無有，歸以問雱，雱言其情，安石咎之。

translations.literal: The emperor showed it to Anshi; Anshi apologized that there was none; returning home he asked Pang, and Pang spoke the truth; Anshi blamed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed it to Wang Anshi; he apologized that there was none; returning home he asked Pang, and Pang spoke the truth; Wang Anshi blamed him.

sentences.zh: 雱憤恚，疽發背死。

translations.literal: Pang, indignant and resentful, developed a carbuncle on his back and died.
translations.idiomatic: Pang, indignant and resentful, developed a carbuncle on his back and died.

sentences.zh: 安石暴綰罪，云「為臣子弟求官及薦臣婿蔡卞」，遂與亨甫皆得罪。

translations.literal: Anshi publicly exposed Wan's crimes, saying he sought office for his clansmen and disciples and recommended his son-in-law Cai Bian; thereupon both he and Hengfu were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi publicly exposed Wan's crimes, saying he sought office for his clansmen and disciples and recommended his son-in-law Cai Bian; thereupon both he and Hengfu were punished.

sentences.zh: 綰始以附安石居言職，及安石與呂惠卿相傾，綰極力助攻惠卿。

translations.literal: Wan at first attached himself to Anshi to hold a remonstrance post; when Anshi and Lü Huiqing contended with each other, Wan exerted himself to the utmost to assist in attacking Huiqing.
translations.idiomatic: Wan at first attached himself to Wang Anshi to hold a remonstrance post; when Wang Anshi and Lü Huiqing contended with each other, Wan exerted himself to the utmost to assist in attacking Huiqing.

sentences.zh: 上頗厭安石所為，綰懼失勢，屢留之於上，其言無所顧忌；

translations.literal: The emperor was quite weary of what Anshi did; Wan feared losing power and repeatedly kept him before the emperor; his words were without any scruple.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was quite weary of what Wang Anshi did; Wan feared losing power and repeatedly kept him before the emperor; his words were without any scruple.

sentences.zh: 亨甫險薄，諂事雱以進，至是皆斥。

translations.literal: Hengfu was treacherous and shallow, fawning on Pang to advance; at this time all were expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Hengfu was treacherous and shallow, fawning on Pang to advance; at this time all were expelled.

sentences.zh: 安石之再相也，屢謝病求去，及子雱死，尤悲傷不堪，力請解幾務。

translations.literal: When Anshi was chief minister again, he repeatedly thanked illness and asked to leave; when his son Pang died, he was especially grief-stricken and unable to bear it, and forcefully asked to be relieved of urgent affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi was chief minister again, he repeatedly pleaded illness and asked to leave; when his son Pang died, he was especially grief-stricken and unable to bear it, and forcefully asked to be relieved of urgent affairs.

sentences.zh: 上益厭之，罷為鎮南軍節度使、同平章事、判江寧府。

translations.literal: The emperor grew ever more weary of him and removed him as Military Commissioner of the Zhennan Army, Associate Grand Councillor, and administrator of Jiangning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew ever more weary of him and removed him as Military Commissioner of the Zhennan Army, Associate Grand Councillor, and administrator of Jiangning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年，改集禧觀使，封舒國公。

translations.literal: The next year he was changed to Commissioner of the Jixi Abbey and enfeoffed as Duke of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was changed to Commissioner of the Jixi Abbey and enfeoffed as Duke of Shu.

sentences.zh: 屢乞還將相印。

translations.literal: He repeatedly asked to return the seals of general and minister.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked to return the seals of general and minister.

sentences.zh: 元豐二年，復拜左僕射、觀文殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanfeng he was again appointed Left Vice Director and Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature.
translations.idiomatic: In 1079 he was again appointed Left Vice Director and Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature.

sentences.zh: 換特進，改封荊。

translations.literal: He was exchanged for Special Advancement and his enfeoffment was changed to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted Special Advancement and his enfeoffment was changed to Jing.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，加司空。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong ascended, he was promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong ascended, he was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，卒，年六十八，贈太傅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou he died, aged sixty-eight, and was posthumously granted Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1086 he died, aged sixty-eight, and was posthumously granted Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，諡曰「文」，配享神宗廟庭。

translations.literal: During Shaosheng he was given the posthumous title Wen and granted a place in sacrificial rites at Emperor Shenzong's temple.
translations.idiomatic: During Shaosheng he was given the posthumous title Wen and granted a place in sacrificial rites at Emperor Shenzong's temple.

sentences.zh: 崇寧三年，又配食文宣王廟，列于顏、孟之次，追封舒王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongning, he was again granted sacrificial honors in the Temple of the Cultured Exemplar King, placed after Yan and Mencius, and posthumously enfeoffed as King of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1104, he was again granted a place in the sacrificial rites at Confucius's temple, ranked after Yan Hui and Mencius, and posthumously enfeoffed as King of Shu.

sentences.zh: 欽宗時，楊時以為言，詔停之。

translations.literal: During the reign of Emperor Qinzong, Yang Shi spoke on the matter, and an edict halted it.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Qinzong's reign, Yang Shi raised the issue, and an edict put a stop to it.

sentences.zh: 高宗用趙鼎、呂聰問言，停宗廟配享，削其王封。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong, acting on the words of Zhao Ding and Lü Congwen, stopped the temple sacrifice and stripped his princely enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong, following the advice of Zhao Ding and Lü Congwen, ended his place in the ancestral temple sacrifices and revoked his princely title.

sentences.zh: 初，安石訓釋《詩》、《書》、《周禮》，既成，頒之學官，天下號曰「新義」。

translations.literal: Initially, Anshi annotated and explained the Odes, Documents, and Rites of Zhou; when finished, they were distributed to the state schools, and the world called them the New Meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, Wang Anshi wrote commentaries on the Classic of Poetry, the Classic of Documents, and the Rites of Zhou. When they were complete, they were issued to the state schools, and the world called them the New Meaning.

sentences.zh: 晚居金陵，又作《字說》，多穿鑿傅會。

translations.literal: In his later years dwelling in Jinling, he also wrote the Explaining Characters, which was full of forced and arbitrary interpretations.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years, living in Jinling, he also wrote the Explaining Characters, which relied heavily on forced and arbitrary readings.

sentences.zh: 其流入於佛、老。

translations.literal: Its influence flowed into Buddhism and Daoism.
translations.idiomatic: Its influence flowed into Buddhism and Daoism.

sentences.zh: 一時學者，無敢不傳習，主司純用以取士，士莫得自名一說，先儒傳注，一切廢不用。

translations.literal: For a time scholars dared not fail to transmit and study them; chief examiners used them exclusively to select officials; scholars could not name a doctrine of their own; traditional Confucian commentaries were entirely abolished and not used.
translations.idiomatic: For a time scholars dared not fail to transmit and study them; chief examiners used them exclusively to select officials; scholars could not advance a doctrine of their own; traditional Confucian commentaries were entirely abolished.

sentences.zh: 黜《春秋》之書，不使列於學官，至戲目為「斷爛朝報」。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals was demoted and not allowed to be listed in the state schools, even mockingly called a 'chopped-up court gazette.'
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals was demoted and excluded from the state schools, even mockingly called a 'chopped-up court gazette.'

sentences.zh: 安石未貴時，名震京師，性不好華腴，自奉至儉，或衣垢不澣，面垢不洗，世多稱其賢。

translations.literal: Before Anshi rose to eminence, his name shook the capital; by nature he did not love luxury, his personal conduct was extremely frugal, sometimes his clothes were soiled unwashed and his face soiled unwashed, and the world mostly praised him as worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Before Wang Anshi rose to eminence, his name shook the capital; by nature he disdained luxury and lived extremely frugally, sometimes wearing unwashed clothes and an unwashed face, and the world mostly praised him as worthy.

sentences.zh: 蜀人蘇洵獨曰：「是不近人情者，鮮不為大奸慝。」

translations.literal: Su Xun of Shu alone said: One who is not close to human feeling rarely fails to become a great villain.
translations.idiomatic: Su Xun of Shu alone said, "One who is not close to human feeling rarely fails to become a great villain."

sentences.zh: 作《辯姦論》以刺之，謂王衍、盧杞合為一人。

translations.literal: He wrote the Discourse on Distinguishing Villainy to satirize him, saying Wang Yan and Lu Qi combined in one person.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Discourse on Distinguishing Villainy to satirize him, saying Wang Yan and Lu Qi combined in one person.

sentences.zh: 安石性強忮，遇事無可否，自信所見，執意不回。

translations.literal: Anshi's nature was strong and jealous; encountering affairs he would neither approve nor disapprove, trusting his own views, holding to his intent without turning back.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi's nature was strong and jealous; encountering affairs he would neither approve nor disapprove, trusting his own views and holding to his intent without turning back.

sentences.zh: 至議變法，而在廷交執不可，安石傅經義，出己意，辯論輒數百言，眾不能詘。

translations.literal: When it came to debating reform, those at court all insisted it could not be done; Anshi applied classical meaning and brought forth his own intent, debating in hundreds of words each time, and none could refute him.
translations.idiomatic: When it came to debating reform, those at court all insisted it could not be done; Wang Anshi applied classical meaning and brought forth his own intent, debating at length each time, and none could refute him.
