sentences.zh: 甚者謂「天變不足畏，祖宗不足法，人言不足恤。」

translations.literal: To an extreme he said: Heavenly changes are not worth fearing, the ancestors are not worth taking as models, people's words are not worth heeding.
translations.idiomatic: To an extreme he said, "Heavenly changes are not worth fearing, the ancestors are not worth taking as models, people's words are not worth heeding."

sentences.zh: 罷黜中外老成人幾盡，多用門下儇慧少年。

translations.literal: He dismissed and expelled mature and established men inside and outside court almost entirely, and mostly used clever young men among his followers.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed and expelled mature and established men inside and outside court almost entirely, and mostly used clever young men among his followers.

sentences.zh: 久之，以旱引去，洎復相，歲餘罷，終神宗世不復召，凡八年。

translations.literal: After a long time he withdrew on account of drought; when he again became chief minister, after a year and more he was removed; through Emperor Shenzong's reign he was never again summoned—for eight years in all.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he withdrew on account of drought; when he again became chief minister, after a year and more he was removed; through Emperor Shenzong's reign he was never again summoned—for eight years in all.

sentences.zh: 子雱。

translations.literal: His son Pang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pang.

sentences.zh: 子 雱

translations.literal: Son: Pang
translations.idiomatic: Son: Pang

sentences.zh: 雱，字元澤。

translations.literal: Pang, styled Yuanze.
translations.idiomatic: Pang, styled Yuanze.

sentences.zh: 為人慓悍陰刻，無所顧忌。

translations.literal: As a man he was fierce, bold, secretive, and cutting, without any scruple.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he was fierce, bold, secretive, and cutting, without any scruple.

sentences.zh: 性敏甚，未冠，已著書數萬言。

translations.literal: His nature was extremely keen; before coming of age he had already written books of tens of thousands of words.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was extremely keen; before coming of age he had already written books of tens of thousands of words.

sentences.zh: 年十三，得秦卒言洮、河事，歎曰：「此可撫而有也。

translations.literal: At age thirteen, hearing a Qin soldier speak of Tao and He affairs, he sighed and said: This can be pacified and possessed.
translations.idiomatic: At age thirteen, hearing a Qin soldier speak of Tao and He affairs, he sighed and said, "This can be pacified and possessed.

sentences.zh: 使西夏得之，則吾敵強而邊患博矣。」

translations.literal: If Western Xia obtains it, then our enemy will be strong and border troubles will be broad.
translations.idiomatic: If Western Xia obtains it, our enemy will grow strong and border troubles will multiply."

sentences.zh: 其後王韶開熙河，安石力主其議，蓋兆於此。

translations.literal: Later when Wang Shao opened the Xihe region, Anshi forcefully led the deliberation—the omen was here.
translations.idiomatic: Later when Wang Shao opened the Xihe region, Wang Anshi forcefully led the deliberation—the omen was here.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，調旌德尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as defender of Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as defender of Jingde.

sentences.zh: 雱氣豪，睥睨一世，不能作小官。

translations.literal: Pang's spirit was bold; he looked down on the age and could not serve as a petty official.
translations.idiomatic: Pang's spirit was bold; he looked down on the age and could not serve as a petty official.

sentences.zh: 作策二十餘篇，極論天下事，又作《老子訓傳》及《佛書義解》，亦數萬言。

translations.literal: He wrote more than twenty policy essays, arguing to the utmost on affairs under Heaven, and also wrote Exegesis and Commentary on the Laozi and Explanations of Buddhist Texts, also tens of thousands of words.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote more than twenty policy essays, arguing to the utmost on affairs under Heaven, and also wrote Exegesis and Commentary on the Laozi and Explanations of Buddhist Texts, also tens of thousands of words.

sentences.zh: 時安石執政，所用多少年，雱亦欲預選，乃與父謀曰：「執政子雖不可預事，而經筵可處。」

translations.literal: At the time Anshi held power and mostly used young men; Pang also wished to be selected in advance, and plotted with his father, saying: A chief minister's son though he cannot participate in affairs, the classics lecture seat can be occupied.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Anshi held power and mostly used young men; Pang also wished to be selected in advance, and plotted with his father, saying, "A chief minister's son though he cannot participate in affairs, the classics lecture seat can be occupied."

sentences.zh: 安石欲上知而自用，乃以雱所作策及注《道德經》鏤板鬻於市，遂傳達於上。

translations.literal: Anshi wished the emperor to know and use him himself, and so had Pang's policy essays and commentary on the Classic of the Way and Virtue carved on blocks and sold in the market, thus reaching the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi wished the emperor to know and use him himself, and so had Pang's policy essays and commentary on the Classic of the Way and Virtue carved on blocks and sold in the market, thus reaching the emperor.

sentences.zh: 鄧綰、曾布又力薦之，召見，除太子中允、崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: Deng Wan and Zeng Bu again forcefully recommended him; he was summoned for an audience and appointed Palace Attendant and Lecturer at the Hall of Esteeming Governance.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan and Zeng Bu again forcefully recommended him; he was summoned for an audience and appointed Palace Attendant and Lecturer at the Hall of Esteeming Governance.

sentences.zh: 神宗數留與語，受詔注《詩》、《書》義，擢天章閣待制兼侍講。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong repeatedly kept him to converse; he received an edict to annotate the meaning of the Odes and Documents and was promoted to Awaiting Orders at the Hall of Heavenly Manifestation and concurrent Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong repeatedly kept him to converse; he received an edict to annotate the meaning of the Odes and Documents and was promoted to Awaiting Orders at the Hall of Heavenly Manifestation and concurrent Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 書成，遷龍圖閣直學士，以病辭不拜。

translations.literal: When the book was complete, he was transferred to Direct Academician of the Hall of Dragon Images; on account of illness he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When the book was complete, he was transferred to Direct Academician of the Hall of Dragon Images; on account of illness he declined and did not accept.

sentences.zh: 安石更張政事，雱實導之。

translations.literal: Anshi reformed government affairs; Pang in fact guided it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi reformed government affairs; Pang in fact guided it.

sentences.zh: 常稱商鞅為豪傑之士，言不誅異議者法不行。

translations.literal: He often called Shang Yang a heroic and outstanding man, saying that unless dissenters were executed the law would not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He often called Shang Yang a heroic and outstanding man, saying that unless dissenters were executed the law would not be carried out.

sentences.zh: 安石與程顥語，雱囚首跣足，攜婦人冠以出，問父所言何事，曰：「以新法數為人所阻，故與程君議。」

translations.literal: Anshi was speaking with Cheng Hao; Pang came out with bound head and bare feet, carrying a woman's cap, and asked what his father was discussing; he said: Because the New Policies are repeatedly blocked by people, I am discussing with Master Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi was speaking with Cheng Hao; Pang came out with bound head and bare feet, carrying a woman's cap, and asked what his father was discussing; he said, "Because the New Policies are repeatedly blocked by people, I am discussing with Master Cheng."

sentences.zh: 雱大言曰：「梟韓琦、富弼之頭於市，則法行矣。」

translations.literal: Pang spoke loudly: Display Han Qi and Fu Bi's heads in the market, and the law will be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Pang spoke loudly, "Display Han Qi and Fu Bi's heads in the market, and the law will be carried out."

sentences.zh: 安石遽曰：「兒誤矣。」

translations.literal: Anshi hastily said: My son is mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi hastily said, "My son is mistaken."

sentences.zh: 卒時才三十三，特贈左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When he died he was only thirty-three; he was specially granted Left Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was only thirty-three; he was specially granted Left Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 唐坰

translations.literal: Tang Jiong
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jiong

translations.literal: 〈Appendix〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Appendix〉

sentences.zh: 唐坰者，以父任得官。

translations.literal: Tang Jiong obtained office through his father's privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jiong obtained office through his father's privilege.

sentences.zh: 熙甯初，上書云：「秦二世制于趙高，乃失之弱，非失之強。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xining he submitted a memorial saying: Qin Ershi was controlled by Zhao Gao—this was a failure of weakness, not a failure of strength.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xining he submitted a memorial saying, "Qin Ershi was controlled by Zhao Gao—this was a failure of weakness, not a failure of strength."

sentences.zh: 神宗悅其言。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong was pleased with his words.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong was pleased with his words.

sentences.zh: 又云：「青苗法不行，宜斬大臣異議如韓琦者數人。」

translations.literal: He also said: If the Green Sprouts Law is not carried out, several great ministers who dissent like Han Qi should be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "If the Green Sprouts Law is not carried out, several great ministers who dissent like Han Qi should be beheaded."

sentences.zh: 安石尤喜之，薦使對，賜進士出身，為崇文校書。

translations.literal: Anshi was especially pleased with him, recommended him for an audience, granted jinshi status, and made him Proofreader of the Chongwen Library.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi was especially pleased with him, recommended him for an audience, granted jinshi status, and made him Proofreader of the Chongwen Library.

sentences.zh: 上薄其人，除知錢塘縣。

translations.literal: The emperor looked down on him as a person and appointed him prefect of Qiantang County.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor looked down on him as a person and appointed him prefect of Qiantang County.

sentences.zh: 安石欲留之，乃令鄧綰薦為御史，遂除太子中允。

translations.literal: Anshi wished to keep him and so had Deng Wan recommend him as censor; he was then appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi wished to keep him and so had Deng Wan recommend him as censor; he was then appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 數月，將用為諫官，安石疑其輕脫，將背己立名，不除職，以本官同知諫院，非故事也。

translations.literal: After several months, when he was about to be used as a remonstrating official, Anshi suspected he was frivolous and would turn against him to make a name; he did not grant the post but made him with his original rank concurrent director of the Remonstrance Academy—not precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After several months, when he was about to be used as a remonstrating official, Wang Anshi suspected he was frivolous and would turn against him to make a name; he did not grant the post but made him with his original rank concurrent director of the Remonstrance Academy—not precedent.

sentences.zh: 坰果怒安石易己，凡奏二十疏，論時事，皆留中不出。

translations.literal: Jiong indeed grew angry that Anshi had slighted him; in all he submitted twenty memorials discussing current affairs, all kept within and not issued.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong indeed grew angry that Wang Anshi had slighted him; in all he submitted twenty memorials discussing current affairs, all kept within and not issued.

sentences.zh: 乃因百官起居日，扣陛請對，上令諭以他日，坰伏地不起，遂召升殿。

translations.literal: Thereupon on the day of officials' attendance he knocked on the steps requesting an audience; the emperor ordered him told another day; Jiong prostrated himself and would not rise, and was then summoned to ascend the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon on the day of officials' attendance he knocked on the steps requesting an audience; the emperor ordered him told another day; Jiong prostrated himself and would not rise, and was then summoned to ascend the hall.

sentences.zh: 坰至御坐前，進曰：「臣所言，皆大臣不法，請對陛下一一陳之。」

translations.literal: Jiong came before the imperial seat and advanced, saying: What your servant speaks of are all great ministers' unlawful acts; I request to state them one by one to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong came before the imperial seat and advanced, saying, "What I speak of are all great ministers' unlawful acts; I request to state them one by one to Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 乃措笏展疏，目安石曰：「王安石近御坐，聽劄子。」

translations.literal: Thereupon he placed his tablet and unfolded his memorial, eyeing Anshi and saying: Wang Anshi, approach the imperial seat and listen to the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he placed his tablet and unfolded his memorial, eyeing Wang Anshi and saying, "Wang Anshi, approach the imperial seat and listen to the memorial."

sentences.zh: 安石遲遲，坰訶曰：「陛下前猶敢如此，在外可知！」

translations.literal: Anshi hesitated; Jiong shouted: Before Your Majesty you still dare to be like this—outside one can imagine!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi hesitated; Jiong shouted, "Before Your Majesty you still dare to be like this—outside one can imagine!"

sentences.zh: 安石悚然而進。

translations.literal: Anshi, startled, advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi, startled, advanced.

sentences.zh: 坰大聲宣讀，凡六十條，大略以「安石專作威福，曾布等表裏擅權，天下但知憚安石威權，不復知有陛下。

translations.literal: Jiong loudly read aloud, in all sixty articles, roughly stating: Anshi monopolizes authority and favor; Zeng Bu and others inside and outside usurp power; all under Heaven knows only to fear Anshi's authority and no longer knows there is Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong loudly read aloud, in all sixty articles, roughly stating, "Wang Anshi monopolizes authority and favor; Zeng Bu and others inside and outside usurp power; all under Heaven knows only to fear Wang Anshi's authority and no longer knows there is Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 文彥博、馮京知而不敢言。

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo and Feng Jing knew but dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo and Feng Jing knew but dared not speak.

sentences.zh: 王珪曲事安石，無異廝僕。」

translations.literal: Wang Gui curried favor with Anshi, no different from a servant.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui curried favor with Wang Anshi, no different from a servant."

sentences.zh: 且讀且目珪，珪慚懼俛首。

translations.literal: As he read he eyed Gui; Gui, ashamed and afraid, bowed his head.
translations.idiomatic: As he read he eyed Gui; Gui, ashamed and afraid, bowed his head.

sentences.zh: 「元絳、薛向、陳繹，安石頤指氣使，無異家奴。

translations.literal: Yuan Jiang, Xue Xiang, and Chen Yi—Anshi orders them with chin and breath like household slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jiang, Xue Xiang, and Chen Yi—Wang Anshi orders them with chin and breath like household slaves.

sentences.zh: 張琥、李定為安石爪牙，臺官張商英乃安石鷹犬。

translations.literal: Zhang Hu and Li Ding are Anshi's claws and teeth; censorate official Zhang Shangying is Anshi's hawk and hound.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hu and Li Ding are Wang Anshi's claws and teeth; censorate official Zhang Shangying is Wang Anshi's hawk and hound.

sentences.zh: 逆意者雖賢為不肖，附己者雖不肖為賢。」

translations.literal: Those who oppose his intent, though worthy, are treated as unworthy; those who attach to him, though unworthy, are treated as worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Those who oppose his intent, though worthy, are treated as unworthy; those who attach to him, though unworthy, are treated as worthy.

sentences.zh: 至詆為李林甫、盧杞。

translations.literal: He even denounced him as Li Linfu and Lu Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He even denounced him as Li Linfu and Lu Qi.

sentences.zh: 上屢止之，坰慷慨自若，略不退懾。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly stopped him; Jiong was passionate and at ease, not retreating or flinching in the least.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly stopped him; Jiong was passionate and at ease, not retreating or flinching in the least.

sentences.zh: 讀已，下殿再拜而退。

translations.literal: When the reading was done, he descended the hall, bowed twice, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the reading was done, he descended the hall, bowed twice, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 侍臣衛士，相顧失色，安石為之請去。

translations.literal: Attendant ministers and guards looked at each other in alarm; Anshi asked to leave on his account.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant ministers and guards looked at each other in alarm; Wang Anshi asked to leave on his account.

sentences.zh: 閣門糾其瀆亂朝儀，貶潮州別駕。

translations.literal: The Gate Office impeached him for profaning and disrupting court ritual; he was demoted to Vice Prefect of Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Office impeached him for profaning and disrupting court ritual; he was demoted to Vice Prefect of Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 鄧綰申救之，且自劾繆舉。

translations.literal: Deng Wan pleaded for him and also impeached himself for mistaken recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan pleaded for him and also impeached himself for mistaken recommendation.

sentences.zh: 安石曰：「此素狂，不足責。」

translations.literal: Anshi said: This one has always been mad—not worth blaming.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said, "This one has always been mad—not worth blaming."

sentences.zh: 改監廣州軍資庫，後徙吉州酒稅，卒官。

translations.literal: He was changed to supervisor of the Guangzhou military supplies storehouse; later transferred to wine tax in Jizhou; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to supervisor of the Guangzhou military supplies storehouse; later transferred to wine tax in Jizhou; he died in office.

sentences.zh: 論曰：朱熹嘗論安石「以文章節行高一世，而尤以道德經濟為己任。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Zhu Xi once discussed Anshi: With literary accomplishment and integrity surpassing his age, and especially taking moral governance and statecraft as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Zhu Xi once discussed Wang Anshi: "With literary accomplishment and integrity surpassing his age, and especially taking moral governance and statecraft as his own charge.

sentences.zh: 被遇神宗，致位宰相，世方仰其有為，庶幾復見二帝三王之盛。

translations.literal: Favored by Emperor Shenzong, he rose to the position of chief minister; the age looked up to his capacity for action, hoping almost to see again the glory of the Two Emperors and Three Kings.
translations.idiomatic: Favored by Emperor Shenzong, he rose to the position of chief minister; the age looked up to his capacity for action, hoping almost to see again the glory of the Two Emperors and Three Kings.

sentences.zh: 而安石乃汲汲以財利兵革為先務，引用凶邪，排擯忠直，躁迫強戾，使天下之人，囂然喪其樂生之心。

translations.literal: Yet Anshi was urgently taking wealth, profit, and military reform as first priorities, employing the vicious and wicked, expelling the loyal and upright, rash, pressing, strong, and perverse, causing the people of all under Heaven clamorously to lose their hearts' joy in living.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wang Anshi was urgently taking wealth, profit, and military reform as first priorities, employing the vicious and wicked, expelling the loyal and upright, rash, pressing, strong, and perverse, causing the people of the realm clamorously to lose their joy in living.

sentences.zh: 卒之群奸嗣虐，流毒四海，至於崇寧、宣和之際，而禍亂極矣」。

translations.literal: In the end wicked men succeeded in cruelty, spreading poison through the four seas, until the era of Chongning and Xuanhe, when calamity and disorder reached its extreme.
translations.idiomatic: In the end wicked men succeeded in cruelty, spreading poison through the four seas, until the era of Chongning and Xuanhe, when calamity and disorder reached its extreme."

sentences.zh: 此天下之公言也。

translations.literal: This is the public word of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: This is the public verdict of the realm.

sentences.zh: 昔神宗欲命相，問韓琦曰：「安石何如？」

translations.literal: Formerly when Emperor Shenzong wished to appoint a chief minister, he asked Han Qi: What of Anshi?
translations.idiomatic: Formerly when Emperor Shenzong wished to appoint a chief minister, he asked Han Qi, "What of Wang Anshi?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「安石為翰林學士則有餘，處輔弼之地則不可。」

translations.literal: He replied: Anshi as Hanlin Academician would be more than sufficient; in the place of assistant and support he would not do.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Wang Anshi as Hanlin Academician would be more than sufficient; in the place of chief minister he would not do."

sentences.zh: 神宗不聽，遂相安石。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong did not listen and thereupon made Anshi chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong did not listen and thereupon made Wang Anshi chief minister.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 此雖宋氏之不幸，亦安石之不幸也。

translations.literal: Though this was the misfortune of the Song house, it was also the misfortune of Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: Though this was the misfortune of the Song house, it was also the misfortune of Wang Anshi.

sentences.zh: 王安禮

translations.literal: Wang Anli
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anli

sentences.zh: 王安禮，字和甫，安石之弟也。

translations.literal: Wang Anli, styled Hefu, was Anshi's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anli, styled Hefu, was Wang Anshi's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 早登科，從河東唐介辟。

translations.literal: He passed the examination early and followed Tang Jie of Hedong as a recruit.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examination early and followed Tang Jie of Hedong as a recruit.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，鄜延路城囉兀，河東發民四萬負餉，宣撫使韓絳檄使佐役，後帥呂公弼將從之。

translations.literal: During Xining, on the Fuyan circuit they fortified Luowu; Hedong mobilized forty thousand people to carry supplies; Pacification Commissioner Han Jiang ordered him to assist in the labor; later Commander Lü Gongbi was about to follow this.
translations.idiomatic: During Xining, on the Fuyan circuit they fortified Luowu; Hedong mobilized forty thousand people to carry supplies; Pacification Commissioner Han Jiang ordered him to assist in the labor; later Commander Lü Gongbi was about to follow this.

sentences.zh: 安禮爭曰：「民兵不習武事，今驅之深入，此不為寇所乘，則凍餓而死爾，宜亟罷遣。」

translations.literal: Anli contested, saying: Militia do not practice military affairs; now driving them deep in—if they are not taken advantage of by bandits, they will die of cold and hunger; they should be quickly dismissed and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Anli contested, saying, "Militia do not practice military affairs; now driving them deep in—if they are not taken advantage of by bandits, they will die of cold and hunger; they should be quickly dismissed and sent back."

sentences.zh: 公弼用其言，民得歸，而他路遇敵者，全軍皆覆。

translations.literal: Gongbi used his words; the people were able to return, while on other routes those who encountered the enemy—the entire army was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Gongbi used his words; the people were able to return, while on other routes those who encountered the enemy—the entire army was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 公弼執安禮手言曰：「四萬之眾，豈偶然哉。

translations.literal: Gongbi took Anli's hand and said: Forty thousand people—is this accidental?
translations.idiomatic: Gongbi took Anli's hand and said, "Forty thousand people—is this accidental?

sentences.zh: 果有陰德，相與共之。」

translations.literal: Truly there is hidden virtue; let us share it together.
translations.idiomatic: Truly there is hidden virtue; let us share it together."

sentences.zh: 初，絳專爵賞，既上最，多失實，公弼以狀聞。

translations.literal: Initially Jiang monopolized enfeoffments and rewards; when he submitted his final report, much was untrue; Gongbi reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Jiang monopolized enfeoffments and rewards; when he submitted his final report, much was untrue; Gongbi reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 詔即河東議功，公弼將受之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered merit to be discussed right in Hedong; Gongbi was about to accept it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered merit to be discussed right in Hedong; Gongbi was about to accept it.

sentences.zh: 安禮曰：「宣撫使以宰相節制諸道，且許便宜，封授一有不韙，人猶得非之。

translations.literal: Anli said: The Pacification Commissioner, as chief minister commanding the circuits, was also permitted discretionary power—if a single enfeoffment or grant was improper, people could still criticize it.
translations.idiomatic: Anli said, "The Pacification Commissioner, as chief minister commanding the circuits, was also permitted discretionary power—if a single enfeoffment or grant was improper, people could still criticize it.

sentences.zh: 公藩臣，乃欲隃進功狀于非其任邪？」

translations.literal: You are a frontier minister—do you wish to secretly advance a merit report beyond your charge?
translations.idiomatic: You are a frontier minister—do you wish to secretly advance a merit report beyond your charge?"

sentences.zh: 公弼遽辭。

translations.literal: Gongbi hastily declined.
translations.idiomatic: Gongbi hastily declined.

sentences.zh: 遂薦安禮於朝，神宗召對，欲驟用之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he recommended Anli to court; Emperor Shenzong summoned him for an audience and wished to promote him rapidly.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he recommended Anli to court; Emperor Shenzong summoned him for an audience and wished to promote him rapidly.

sentences.zh: 安石當國，辭，以為著作佐郎、崇文院校書。

translations.literal: Anshi was directing the state; Anli declined and was made Assistant Editor and Proofreader of the Chongwen Library.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi was directing the state; Anli declined and was made Assistant Editor and Proofreader of the Chongwen Library.

sentences.zh: 他日得見，命之坐，有司言八品官無賜坐者，特命之。

translations.literal: On another day when he received an audience, the emperor ordered him seated; the officials said that eighth-rank officials were not granted seats—the emperor specially ordered it.
translations.idiomatic: On another day when he received an audience, the emperor ordered him seated. The officials said that eighth-rank officials were not granted seats, but the emperor specially ordered it.

sentences.zh: 遷直集賢院，出知潤州、湖州，召為開封府判官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Directorship of the Jixian Academy, went out as prefect of Run and Hu prefectures, and was recalled as vice prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Directorship of the Jixian Academy, went out as prefect of Run and Hu prefectures, and was recalled as vice prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 嘗偕尹奏事，既退，獨留訪以天下事，帝甚鄉納。

translations.literal: Once when he appeared with the prefect to report on affairs, after withdrawing he alone was kept behind and questioned about affairs under Heaven; the emperor was greatly inclined to accept his views.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he appeared with the prefect to report on affairs, after withdrawing he alone was kept behind and questioned about affairs under Heaven; the emperor was greatly inclined to accept his views.

sentences.zh: 直舍人院、同修起居注。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Academy and concurrent Compiler of the Daily Record.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Academy and concurrent Compiler of the Daily Record.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾下御史獄，勢危甚，無敢救者。

translations.literal: When Su Shi was imprisoned by the censorate, his situation was extremely perilous and none dared rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Shi was imprisoned by the censorate, his situation was extremely perilous and none dared rescue him.

sentences.zh: 安禮從容言：「自古大度之主，不以言語罪人。

translations.literal: Anli said calmly: Since ancient times, magnanimous rulers have not punished people for their words.
translations.idiomatic: Anli said calmly, "Since ancient times, magnanimous rulers have not punished people for their words.

sentences.zh: 軾以才自奮，謂爵位可立取，顧錄錄如此，其心不能無觖望。

translations.literal: Shi relied on his talent to exert himself, thinking rank and title could be quickly obtained; yet he ended up like this, and his heart could not be without resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Shi relied on his talent to exert himself, thinking rank and title could be quickly obtained; yet he ended up like this, and his heart could not be without resentment.

sentences.zh: 今一旦致於理，恐後世謂陛下不能容才。」

translations.literal: Now if he is suddenly brought to justice, I fear later ages will say Your Majesty cannot tolerate talent.
translations.idiomatic: Now if he is suddenly brought to justice, I fear later ages will say Your Majesty cannot tolerate talent."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕固不深譴也，行為卿貰之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: I in fact will not deeply punish him; soon I will pardon him for your sake.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I in fact will not deeply punish him; soon I will pardon him for your sake.

sentences.zh: 卿第去，勿漏言，軾方賈怨於眾，恐言者緣以害卿也。」

translations.literal: You just go and do not leak a word; Shi is just now buying resentment from the crowd—I fear speakers will use this to harm you.
translations.idiomatic: You just go and do not leak a word; Shi is just now buying resentment from the crowd—I fear critics will use this to harm you."

sentences.zh: 李定、張璪皆擿使勿救，安禮不答，軾以故得輕比。

translations.literal: Li Ding and Zhang Zao both prodded him not to rescue; Anli did not reply; Shi for this reason received a light sentence.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ding and Zhang Zao both prodded him not to rescue; Anli did not reply; Shi for this reason received a light sentence.

sentences.zh: 進知制誥。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Drafter of Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Drafter of Edicts.

sentences.zh: 彗星見，詔求直言。

translations.literal: A comet appeared; an edict sought forthright speech.
translations.idiomatic: A comet appeared; an edict sought forthright speech.

sentences.zh: 安禮上疏曰：「人事失於下，變象見於上。

translations.literal: Anli submitted a memorial saying: Human affairs fail below, and change-omens appear above.
translations.idiomatic: Anli submitted a memorial saying, "Human affairs fail below, and change-omens appear above.

sentences.zh: 陛下有仁民愛物之心，而澤不下究，意者左右大臣不均不直，謂忠者為不忠，不賢者為賢，乘權射利者，用力殫於溝瘠，取利究於園夫，足以干陰陽而召星變。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has a heart that cherishes the people and loves things, yet grace does not reach to the bottom—I suspect the great ministers at your side are uneven and not upright, calling the loyal disloyal and the unworthy worthy; those who seize power to pursue profit exhaust their strength on the emaciated in ditches and extract profit to the utmost from gardeners—enough to disturb yin and yang and summon star changes.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has a heart that cherishes the people and loves things, yet grace does not reach to the bottom—I suspect the great ministers at your side are uneven and not upright, calling the loyal disloyal and the unworthy worthy; those who seize power to pursue profit exhaust their strength on the emaciated in ditches and extract profit to the utmost from gardeners—enough to disturb yin and yang and summon star changes.

sentences.zh: 願察親近之行，杜邪枉之門。

translations.literal: I wish that Your Majesty would examine the conduct of those close to you and block the gate of wicked perversity.
translations.idiomatic: I wish that Your Majesty would examine the conduct of those close to you and block the gate of wicked perversity.

sentences.zh: 至於祈禳小數，貶損舊章，恐非所以應天者。」

translations.literal: As for petty prayers and aversions, and demoting old regulations—I fear these are not the way to respond to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: As for petty prayers and aversions, and demoting old regulations—I fear these are not the way to respond to Heaven."

sentences.zh: 帝覽數嘉歎，諭之曰：「王珪欲使卿條具，朕嘗謂不應沮格人言，以自壅障。

translations.literal: The emperor read it several times with praise and sighs, and instructed him: Wang Gui wished you to itemize in detail; I once said one should not obstruct and block people's words to self-obstruct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it several times with praise and sighs, and instructed him, "Wang Gui wished you to itemize in detail; I once said one should not obstruct and block people's words to self-obstruct.

sentences.zh: 今以一指蔽目，雖泰、華在前弗之見，近習蔽其君，何以異此，卿當益自信。」

translations.literal: Now to cover the eyes with one finger—even with Mount Tai and Mount Hua before one, one does not see them; close attendants obscuring their ruler—how is this different? You should be ever more confident.
translations.idiomatic: Now to cover the eyes with one finger—even with Mount Tai and Mount Hua before one, one does not see them; close attendants obscuring their ruler—how is this different? You should be ever more confident."

sentences.zh: 以翰林學士知開封府，事至立斷。

translations.literal: As Hanlin Academician he administered Kaifeng Prefecture; when affairs arrived he decided them on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: As Hanlin Academician he administered Kaifeng Prefecture; when affairs arrived he decided them on the spot.

sentences.zh: 前滯訟不得其情，及且按而未論者幾萬人，安禮剖決，未三月，三獄院及畿、赤十九邑，囚繫皆空。

translations.literal: Previously stalled lawsuits whose facts were not obtained, and those detained awaiting judgment, numbered nearly ten thousand; Anli judged and decided them; within not three months, the three prison courts and the nineteen districts of the capital region and red districts—all prisoners were empty.
translations.idiomatic: Previously stalled lawsuits whose facts were not obtained, and those detained awaiting judgment, numbered nearly ten thousand; Anli judged and decided them; within not three months, the three prison courts and the nineteen districts of the capital region—all prisoners were released.

sentences.zh: 書揭於府前，遼使過而見之，歎息誇異。

translations.literal: The notice was posted before the prefecture; a Liao envoy passed and saw it, sighing and praising it as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: The notice was posted before the prefecture; a Liao envoy passed and saw it, sighing and praising it as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，喜曰：「昔秦內史廖從容俎豆，以奪由余之謀，今安禮能勤吏事，駭動殊鄰，于古無愧矣。」

translations.literal: When the emperor heard it, he said with pleasure: Formerly Qin's Interior Scribe Liao, at ease with ritual vessels, took away Youyu's stratagem; now Anli can diligently manage official affairs and startle distant neighbors—in antiquity he would be without shame.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard it, he said with pleasure, "Formerly Qin's Interior Scribe Liao, at ease with ritual vessels, took away Youyu's stratagem; now Anli can diligently manage official affairs and startle distant neighbors—in antiquity he would be without shame."

sentences.zh: 特升一階。

translations.literal: He was specially promoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 帝數失皇子，太史言民墓多迫京城，故不利國嗣，詔悉改卜，無虜數十萬計，眾洶懼。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly lost imperial sons; the Grand Astrologer said common people's graves mostly pressed on the capital, hence unfavorable to the imperial heir; an edict ordered all to be reburied—captives numbered in the hundreds of thousands; the crowd was in uproar and fear.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly lost imperial sons; the Grand Astrologer said common people's graves mostly pressed on the capital, hence unfavorable to the imperial heir; an edict ordered all to be reburied—graves numbered in the hundreds of thousands; the crowd was in uproar and fear.

sentences.zh: 安禮諫曰：「文王卜世三十，其政先於掩骼埋胔，未聞遷人之塚以利其嗣者。」

translations.literal: Anli remonstrated, saying: King Wen divined thirty generations for his house; his government put first covering exposed bones and burying flesh—I have never heard of moving people's graves to benefit one's heir.
translations.idiomatic: Anli remonstrated, saying, "King Wen divined thirty generations for his house; his government put first covering exposed bones and burying flesh—I have never heard of moving people's graves to benefit one's heir."

sentences.zh: 帝惻然而罷。

translations.literal: The emperor, moved to compassion, stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, moved to compassion, stopped it.

sentences.zh: 邏者連得匿名書告人不軌，所涉百餘家。

translations.literal: Patrol officers continuously obtained anonymous letters reporting people's misconduct; more than a hundred households were involved.
translations.idiomatic: Patrol officers continuously obtained anonymous letters reporting people's misconduct; more than a hundred households were involved.

sentences.zh: 帝付安禮曰：「亟治之。」

translations.literal: The emperor handed it to Anli, saying: Quickly investigate it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor handed it to Anli, saying, "Quickly investigate it."

sentences.zh: 安禮驗所指，皆略同，最後一書加三人，有姓薛者，安禮喜曰：「吾得之矣。」

translations.literal: Anli verified those indicated—all were roughly the same; the last letter added three people, one surnamed Xue; Anli said with pleasure: I have got it.
translations.idiomatic: Anli verified those indicated—all were roughly the same; the last letter added three people, one surnamed Xue; Anli said with pleasure, "I have got it."

sentences.zh: 呼問薛曰：「若豈有素不快者耶？」

translations.literal: He called and asked Xue: Do you perhaps have someone with whom you have long been displeased?
translations.idiomatic: He called and asked Xue, "Do you perhaps have someone with whom you have long been displeased?"

sentences.zh: 曰有持筆來售者，拒之，鞅鞅去，其意似見銜。

translations.literal: He said there was one who came selling brushes; he refused him; the man left resentfully—his intent seemed to show grievance.
translations.idiomatic: He said there was one who came selling brushes; he refused him; the man left resentfully—his intent seemed to show grievance.

sentences.zh: 即命捕訊，果其所為也。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered arrest and interrogation; it was indeed his doing.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered arrest and interrogation; it was indeed his doing.

sentences.zh: 即梟其首於市，不逮一人，京師謂為神明。

translations.literal: He immediately displayed the man's head in the market; not one person was implicated; the capital called him divine.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately displayed the man's head in the market; not one person was implicated; the capital called him divine.

sentences.zh: 宗室令騑以數十萬錢買妾，久而斥歸之，訴府督元直。

translations.literal: A clansman, Commandant Fei, bought a concubine for several hundred thousand cash; after a long time he dismissed and returned her; she sued the prefecture to compel return of the original price.
translations.idiomatic: A clansman, Commandant Fei, bought a concubine for several hundred thousand cash; after a long time he dismissed and returned her; she sued the prefecture to compel return of the original price.

sentences.zh: 安禮視妾，既火敗其面矣，即奏言：「妾之所以直數十萬者，以姿首也，今炙敗之，則不復可鬻，此與炮烙之刑何異。

translations.literal: Anli looked at the concubine—her face had already been burned and ruined; he immediately memorialized: The reason the concubine was worth several hundred thousand was her appearance; now having burned and ruined it, she can no longer be sold—how is this different from the branding torture?
translations.idiomatic: Anli looked at the concubine—her face had already been burned and ruined; he immediately memorialized, "The reason the concubine was worth several hundred thousand was her appearance; now having burned and ruined it, she can no longer be sold—how is this different from the branding torture?

sentences.zh: 請勿理其直而加厚譴，以為戒。」

translations.literal: I request that the original price not be adjudicated but that heavy punishment be added as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: I request that the original price not be adjudicated but that heavy punishment be added as a warning."

sentences.zh: 詔從之，仍奪令騑俸。

translations.literal: An edict followed this and moreover stripped Commandant Fei of his salary.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed this and moreover stripped Commandant Fei of his salary.

sentences.zh: 後宮造油箔，約三年損者反其價，才一年有損者，中官持詣府，請如約，詞氣甚厲。

translations.literal: The inner palace made oil paper; it was agreed that if damaged within three years the price would be returned; after only one year there was damage; an inner attendant brought it to the prefecture requesting according to the agreement, his tone very fierce.
translations.idiomatic: The inner palace made oil paper; it was agreed that if damaged within three years the price would be returned; after only one year there was damage; an inner attendant brought it to the prefecture requesting according to the agreement, his tone very fierce.

sentences.zh: 安禮曰：「庸詎非置之不得其地，為風雨燥濕所壞耶。

translations.literal: Anli said: Could it not be that it was not placed in the proper place and was damaged by wind, rain, dryness, and damp?
translations.idiomatic: Anli said, "Could it not be that it was not placed in the proper place and was damaged by wind, rain, dryness, and damp?

sentences.zh: 苟如是，民將無復得直，約不可用也。」

translations.literal: If it is so, the people will never again get their price back—the agreement cannot be used.
translations.idiomatic: If it is so, the people will never again get their price back—the agreement cannot be used."

sentences.zh: 卒不追。

translations.literal: In the end he did not pursue it.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not pursue it.

sentences.zh: 以是宗室、中貴人皆憚之。

translations.literal: Because of this the clansmen and inner favorites all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this the clansmen and inner favorites all feared him.

sentences.zh: 元豐四年，初分三省，置執政，拜中大夫、尚書右丞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanfeng, when the Three Departments were first divided and chief ministers were established, he was appointed Grandee of Palace Attendance and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1081, when the Three Departments were first divided and chief ministers were established, he was appointed Grandee of Palace Attendance and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 轉左丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 王師問罪夏國，涇原承受梁同奏：「轉運使葉康直餉米，惡不可食。」

translations.literal: The imperial army demanded punishment of the Xia state; Liang Tong, receiver on the Jingyuan circuit, memorialized: Transport Commissioner Ye Kangzhi's supply grain was foul and inedible.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army demanded punishment of the Xia state; Liang Tong, receiver on the Jingyuan circuit, memorialized, "Transport Commissioner Ye Kangzhi's supply grain was foul and inedible."

sentences.zh: 帝大怒曰：「貴糴遠餉，反不可用。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angry and said: Buying dear and supplying from afar—yet it cannot be used.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly angry and said, "Buying dear and supplying from afar—yet it cannot be used.

sentences.zh: 徒弊民力于道路，康直可斬也。」

translations.literal: Merely wasting the people's strength on the roads—Kangzhi can be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Merely wasting the people's strength on the roads—Kangzhi can be beheaded."

sentences.zh: 安禮曰：「此一梁同之言，疑未必實，當按之。」

translations.literal: Anli said: This is only Liang Tong's word—I suspect it may not be true; it should be investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Anli said, "This is only Liang Tong's word—I suspect it may not be true; it should be investigated."

sentences.zh: 乃遣判官張大寧與同參核，且械繫康直以俟。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dispatched Vice Director Zhang Daning to jointly verify with Tong, and moreover shackled and detained Kangzhi to await results.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he dispatched Vice Director Zhang Daning to jointly verify with Tong, and moreover shackled and detained Kangzhi to await results.

sentences.zh: 既而米可用者什八九，帝意解，赦康直。

translations.literal: Afterward eight or nine tenths of the grain was usable; the emperor's mind was relieved and Kangzhi was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward eight or nine tenths of the grain was usable; the emperor's mind was relieved and Kangzhi was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 是時，伐夏不得志，李憲又欲再舉。

translations.literal: At this time the campaign against Xia had not succeeded; Li Xian again wished to launch another.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the campaign against Xia had not succeeded; Li Xian again wished to launch another.

sentences.zh: 帝以訪輔臣，王珪曰：「向所患者用不足，朝廷今捐錢鈔五百萬緡，以供軍食有餘矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor consulted the assistant ministers; Wang Gui said: What we previously worried about was insufficient expenditure; the court now contributes five million strings of cash notes—enough to supply army provisions with surplus.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted the assistant ministers; Wang Gui said, "What we previously worried about was insufficient expenditure; the court now contributes five million strings of cash notes—enough to supply army provisions with surplus."

sentences.zh: 安禮曰：「鈔不可啖，必變而為錢，錢又變為芻粟。

translations.literal: Anli said: Notes cannot be eaten—they must be converted to cash, and cash must be converted to fodder and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Anli said, "Notes cannot be eaten—they must be converted to cash, and cash must be converted to fodder and grain.

sentences.zh: 今距出征之期才兩月，安能集事。」

translations.literal: Now until the date of the expedition there are only two months—how can the matter be gathered?
translations.idiomatic: Now until the date of the expedition there are only two months—how can the matter be gathered in time?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「李憲以為已有備，彼宦者能如是，卿等獨無意乎？

translations.literal: The emperor said: Li Xian thinks he is already prepared—if that eunuch can be like this, do you alone have no intent?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Li Xian thinks he is already prepared—if that eunuch can be like this, do you alone have no intent?

sentences.zh: 唐平淮蔡，唯裴度謀議與主同。

translations.literal: When Tang pacified Huai and Cai, only Pei Du's plans and deliberations agreed with the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang pacified Huai and Cai, only Pei Du's plans and deliberations agreed with the ruler.

sentences.zh: 今乃不出公卿而出於閹寺，朕甚恥之。」

translations.literal: Now it does not come from dukes and ministers but from eunuch offices—I am greatly shamed by this.
translations.idiomatic: Now it does not come from dukes and ministers but from eunuch offices—I am greatly shamed by this."

sentences.zh: 安禮曰：「淮西，三州爾，有裴度之謀，李光顏、李愬之將，然猶引天下之兵力，歷歲而後定。

translations.literal: Anli said: Huaixi was only three prefectures; there were Pei Du's plans and the generals Li Guangyan and Li Su—yet still the military strength of all under Heaven was drawn, and only after years was it settled.
translations.idiomatic: Anli said, "Huaixi was only three prefectures; there were Pei Du's plans and the generals Li Guangyan and Li Su—yet still the military strength of the realm was drawn, and only after years was it settled.

sentences.zh: 今夏氏之強非淮蔡比，憲材非度匹，諸將非有光顏、愬輩，臣懼無以副聖意也。」

translations.literal: Now the Xia house's strength is not comparable to Huai and Cai; Xian's talent is not Pei Du's match; the generals do not have men like Guangyan and Su—I fear I cannot fulfill the sage intent.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Xia state's strength is not comparable to Huai and Cai; Xian's talent is not Pei Du's match; the generals do not have men like Guangyan and Su—I fear we cannot fulfill Your Majesty's intent."

sentences.zh: 帝悟而止。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood and stopped.

sentences.zh: 後欲除憲節度使，安禮又以為不可。

translations.literal: Later when they wished to appoint Xian military commissioner, Anli again thought it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Later when they wished to appoint Xian military commissioner, Anli again thought it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞舒亶上章詆執政，且言：「尚書不置錄目，有旨按吏罪。」

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Shu Dan submitted a memorial slandering those in power, and also said: The Department of State Affairs did not establish a record register—there was an order to investigate officials' crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Shu Dan submitted a memorial slandering those in power, and also said, "The Department of State Affairs did not establish a record register—there was an order to investigate officials' crimes."

sentences.zh: 安禮請取臺錄以為式，乃與省中同，遂並列亶他事，亶坐廢。

translations.literal: Anli requested taking the censorate record as the model—it was the same as in the secretariat; thereupon he also listed Dan's other affairs, and Dan was punished and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Anli requested taking the censorate record as the model—it was the same as in the secretariat; thereupon he also listed Dan's other affairs, and Dan was punished and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 徐禧計議邊事，安禮曰：「禧志大才疏，必誤國。」

translations.literal: Xu Xi planned and deliberated on border affairs; Anli said: Xi's ambition is great but his talent sparse—he will surely harm the state.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xi planned and deliberated on border affairs; Anli said, "Xi's ambition is great but his talent sparse—he will surely harm the state."

sentences.zh: 及永樂敗書聞，帝曰：「安禮每勸朕勿用兵，少置獄，蓋為是也。」

translations.literal: When news of the defeat at Yongle arrived, the emperor said: Anli always urged me not to use troops and to establish fewer prisons—it was probably for this.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the defeat at Yongle arrived, the emperor said, "Anli always urged me not to use troops and to establish fewer prisons—it was probably for this."

sentences.zh: 久之，御史張汝賢論其過，以端明殿學士知江寧府，汝賢亦罷。

translations.literal: After a long time Censor Zhang Ruxian discussed his faults; he was made Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Clarity and prefect of Jiangning; Ruxian was also dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time Censor Zhang Ruxian discussed his faults; he was made Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Clarity and prefect of Jiangning; Ruxian was also dismissed.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，加資政殿學士，歷揚、青、蔡三州。

translations.literal: During Yuanyou he was promoted to Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and served in the three prefectures of Yang, Qing, and Cai.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanyou he was promoted to Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and served in the three prefectures of Yang, Qing, and Cai.

sentences.zh: 又為御史言，失學士，移舒州。

translations.literal: Again on a censor's word he lost his academician rank and was transferred to Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Again on a censor's word he lost his academician rank and was transferred to Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，還職，知永興軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng he returned to his post and administered Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shaosheng he returned to his post and administered Yongxing Army.

sentences.zh: 二年，知太原府。

translations.literal: In the second year he administered Taiyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he administered Taiyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 苦風痹，臥帳中決事，下不敢欺。

translations.literal: He suffered from wind paralysis; lying in his tent he decided affairs, and subordinates dared not deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: He suffered from wind paralysis; lying in his tent he decided affairs, and subordinates dared not deceive him.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十二，贈右銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-two, and was posthumously granted Right Silver-Gleaming Grandee of Glorious Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died, aged sixty-two, and was posthumously granted Right Silver-Gleaming Grandee of Glorious Affairs.

sentences.zh: 安禮偉風儀，論議明辨，常以經綸自任，而闊略細謹，以故數詒口語云。

translations.literal: Anli had a grand bearing; his discourse was clear and discerning; he often took statecraft as his own charge, yet was broad and negligent in minute care—therefore he repeatedly gave cause for gossip.
translations.idiomatic: Anli had a grand bearing; his discourse was clear and discerning; he often took statecraft as his own charge, yet was broad and negligent in minute care—therefore he repeatedly gave cause for gossip.

sentences.zh: 王安國

translations.literal: Wang Anguo
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anguo

sentences.zh: 王安國，字平甫，安禮之弟也。

translations.literal: Wang Anguo, styled Pingfu, was Anli's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anguo, styled Pingfu, was Anli's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 幼敏悟，未嘗從學，而文詞天成。

translations.literal: From youth he was keen and perceptive; he never studied formally, yet his literary words were naturally formed.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was keen and perceptive; he never studied formally, yet his literary words came naturally.

sentences.zh: 年十二，出所為詩、銘、論、賦數十篇示人，語皆警拔，遂以文章聞于世，士大夫交口譽之。

translations.literal: At age twelve he produced several tens of poems, inscriptions, discourses, and rhapsodies he had written to show people; the language was all striking and elevated, and he thereby became known to the world for his literary works; officials and gentry praised him with one voice.
translations.idiomatic: At age twelve he produced several tens of poems, inscriptions, discourses, and rhapsodies he had written to show people; the language was all striking and elevated, and he thereby became known to the world for his literary works; officials and gentry praised him with one voice.

sentences.zh: 於書無所不通，數舉進士，又舉茂材異等，有司考其所獻序言為第一，以母喪不試，廬於墓三年。

translations.literal: In books there was nothing he did not master; he repeatedly passed the jinshi examination and also passed the Exceptional Talent examination; the officials judged his submitted preface first; on account of mourning for his mother he did not test and built a hut at the grave for three years.
translations.idiomatic: In books there was nothing he did not master; he repeatedly passed the jinshi examination and also passed the Exceptional Talent examination; the officials judged his submitted preface first; on account of mourning for his mother he did not test and built a hut at the grave for three years.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，韓絳薦其材行，召試，賜及第，除西京國子教授。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xining Han Jiang recommended his talent and conduct; he was summoned for testing, granted passing rank, and appointed Professor of the Western Capital Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xining Han Jiang recommended his talent and conduct; he was summoned for testing, granted passing rank, and appointed Professor of the Western Capital Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 官滿，至京師，上以安石故，賜對。

translations.literal: When his term was complete he came to the capital; because of Anshi the emperor granted him an audience.
translations.idiomatic: When his term was complete he came to the capital; because of Wang Anshi the emperor granted him an audience.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿學問通古今，以漢文帝為何如主？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: Your learning extends through antiquity and the present—what kind of ruler was Emperor Wen of Han?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your learning extends through antiquity and the present—what kind of ruler was Emperor Wen of Han?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「三代以後未有也。」

translations.literal: He replied: Since the Three Dynasties there has been none like him.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Since the Three Dynasties there has been none like him."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「但恨其才不能立法更制爾。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: I only regret that his talent could not establish laws and change institutions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I only regret that his talent could not establish laws and change institutions."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「文帝自代來，入未央宮，定變故俄頃呼吸間，恐無才者不能。

translations.literal: He replied: From the time Wen came from Dai, entered Weiyang Palace, and settled the crisis in a moment between breaths—I fear one without talent could not have done it.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "From the time Wen came from Dai, entered Weiyang Palace, and settled the crisis in a moment between breaths—I fear one without talent could not have done it.

sentences.zh: 至用賈誼言，待群臣有節，專務以德化民，海內興於禮義，幾致刑措，則文帝加有才一等矣。」

translations.literal: As for using Jia Yi's words, treating the ministers with measure, devoting himself to transforming the people through virtue, raising ritual and righteousness throughout the realm, almost achieving the laying aside of punishments—then Wen was one degree more talented.
translations.idiomatic: As for using Jia Yi's words, treating the ministers with measure, devoting himself to transforming the people through virtue, raising ritual and righteousness throughout the realm, almost achieving the laying aside of punishments—then Wen was one degree more talented."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「王猛佐苻堅，以蕞爾國而令必行，今朕以天下之大，不能使人，何也？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: Wang Meng assisted Fu Jian—with a tiny state yet orders were surely carried out; now I with the vastness of all under Heaven cannot make people obey—why?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Wang Meng assisted Fu Jian—with a tiny state yet orders were surely carried out; now I with the vastness of the realm cannot make people obey—why?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「猛教堅以峻刑法殺人，致秦祚不傳世，今刻薄小人，必有以是誤陛下者。

translations.literal: He said: Meng taught Jian to kill people with harsh punishments, causing Qin's fortune not to pass to another generation; now harsh petty men—there must be those who will use this to mislead Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Meng taught Jian to kill people with harsh punishments, causing Qin's fortune not to pass to another generation; now harsh petty men—there must be those who will use this to mislead Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 願顓以堯、舜、三代為法，則下豈有不從者乎。」

translations.literal: I wish that you would exclusively take Yao, Shun, and the Three Dynasties as models—then would those below have any who would not follow?
translations.idiomatic: I wish that you would exclusively take Yao, Shun, and the Three Dynasties as models—then would those below have any who would not follow?"

sentences.zh: 又問：「卿兄秉政，外論謂何？」

translations.literal: He again asked: Your elder brother holds power—what do outside opinions say?
translations.idiomatic: He again asked, "Your elder brother holds power—what do outside opinions say?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「恨知人不明，聚斂太急爾。」

translations.literal: He said: They regret that he does not know people clearly and that he collects revenue too urgently.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "They regret that he does not know people clearly and that he collects revenue too urgently."

sentences.zh: 帝默然不悅，由是別無恩命，止授崇文院校書，後改秘閣校理。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent and displeased; from this there was no other gracious appointment—he was only made Proofreader of the Chongwen Library, later changed to Collator of the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was silent and displeased; from this there was no other gracious appointment—he was only made Proofreader of the Chongwen Library, later changed to Collator of the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 屢以新法力諫安石，又質責曾布誤其兄，深惡呂惠卿之奸。

translations.literal: He repeatedly remonstrated with Anshi using the New Policies as leverage, also directly reproached Zeng Bu for misleading his elder brother, and deeply hated Lü Huiqing's wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly remonstrated with Wang Anshi using the New Policies as leverage, also directly reproached Zeng Bu for misleading his elder brother, and deeply hated Lü Huiqing's wickedness.

sentences.zh: 先是，安國教授西京，頗溺于聲色，安石在相位，以書戒之曰：「宜放鄭聲。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Anguo was professor in the Western Capital, he was quite immersed in music and women; Anshi in the chief minister's position admonished him in a letter: You should abandon the music of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Anguo was professor in the Western Capital, he was quite immersed in music and women; Wang Anshi in the chief minister's position admonished him in a letter, "You should abandon the music of Zheng."

sentences.zh: 安國復書曰「亦願兄遠佞人。」

translations.literal: Anguo replied in a letter: I also wish my elder brother would keep far from flatterers.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo replied in a letter, "I also wish my elder brother would keep far from flatterers."

sentences.zh: 惠卿銜之。

translations.literal: Huiqing harbored resentment over this.
translations.idiomatic: Huiqing harbored resentment over this.

sentences.zh: 及安石罷相，惠卿遂因鄭俠事陷安國，坐奪官，放歸田里，詔以諭安石，安石對使者泣下。

translations.literal: When Anshi was removed as chief minister, Huiqing thereupon used the Zheng Xia affair to trap Anguo; he was punished by stripping of office and sent back to the countryside; an edict was sent to inform Anshi, and Anshi wept before the messenger.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi was removed as chief minister, Huiqing thereupon used the Zheng Xia affair to trap Anguo; he was punished by stripping of office and sent back to the countryside; an edict was sent to inform Wang Anshi, and he wept before the messenger.

sentences.zh: 既而復其官，命下而安國卒，年四十七。

translations.literal: Soon afterward his office was restored; the order was issued but Anguo died, aged forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his office was restored; the order was issued but Anguo died, aged forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 論曰：安石惡蘇軾而安禮救之，昵惠卿而安國折之，議者不以咎二弟也，惟其當而已矣。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Anshi hated Su Shi yet Anli rescued him; he was close to Huiqing yet Anguo rebuked him—critics do not blame the two younger brothers; they acted only as was appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Wang Anshi hated Su Shi yet Anli rescued him; he was close to Huiqing yet Anguo rebuked him—critics do not blame the two younger brothers; they acted only as was appropriate.

sentences.zh: 安禮為政，有足稱者。

translations.literal: Anli in governing had what is worth praising.
translations.idiomatic: Anli in governing had what is worth praising.

sentences.zh: 安國早卒，故不見於用云。

translations.literal: Anguo died early, and so was not seen in employment.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo died early, and so was not seen in employment.
